data.title: RisingWave: An Open‑Source Stream‑Processing and Management Platform
data.author: Sheldon_fun
data.article_summary:
RisingWave是一个流处理与管理平台，旨在以最简单且最具成本效益的方式处理、分析和管理实时事件数据，支持Apache Iceberg™开放表格式。它提供兼容PostgreSQL的SQL接口和DataFrame风格的Python接口，能够每秒处理数百万事件，进行实时流数据和历史数据的连接与分析，支持低延迟的即席查询，并将结果持久化到Apache Iceberg™或其他下游系统。

RisingWave的关键特性包括：
- 高吞吐量：每秒处理百万级事件。
- 实时处理：增量处理实时和历史数据。
- 低延迟查询：支持即席查询。
- 内置存储：支持Apache Iceberg™，实现低成本数据存储和开放访问。

其设计优势在于：
- PostgreSQL兼容性：支持熟悉的SQL语法。
- 无需手动调优：简化状态管理。
- 使用S3作为主要存储：提供高性能和快速恢复能力，支持动态扩展。
- 弹性磁盘缓存：优化性能并降低成本。

RisingWave适用于流式分析和事件驱动应用等场景，如股票交易、体育博彩和物联网监控。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：RisingWave及类似工具（如Materialize、ClickHouse）在实际应用中的价值和使用场景。

不同观点：
• **up2isomorphism** 认为当前已经有太多类似工具，对人们继续涌入这个领域表示不解，暗示市场可能已经饱和。
• **jsumrall** 对RisingWave和Materialize表示了初步的好感，尤其对RisingWave团队有正面印象。不过最终选择了ClickHouse，因为其物化视图功能易于设置且性能良好，相比之下Timescale虽然性能不错但需要更多专业知识。
• **synthc** 希望了解RisingWave在实际生产环境中的表现，表明目前缺乏相关经验报告。
• **rubenvanwyk** 对RisingWave的实际用例感到好奇，特别是除了实时分析和可观察性之外，是否还有人将其用于增量视图维护（如在Postgres中）。
• **vivzkestrel** 提出一个基础性问题，即在什么情况下应该选择RisingWave或Kafka这样的系统，而不是传统的Redis PubSub系统。
• **shepardrtc** 对RisingWave的架构图表示赞赏，并询问使用了什么工具来制作。
• **esafak** 对RisingWave作为基于Rust的Flink简化版表示疑问，质疑其是否真的更简单。
• **acjohnson55** 直接比较RisingWave和Materialize，希望了解两者之间的优劣。

补充讨论：
• 关于RisingWave的生产环境经验报告较少，用户对其实际表现存在疑问（synthc）。
• 用户对RisingWave的实际应用场景有不同看法，有人关注其在Postgres中增量视图维护的潜力（rubenvanwyk）。
• 基础性比较，如与传统Redis PubSub的对比，显示出对何时选择复杂系统与简单系统的困惑（vivzkestrel）。
• 架构图的制作工具引发关注，显示出对技术展示方式的兴趣（shepardrtc）。
• RisingWave与Materialize的直接对比显示出用户在选择类似工具时的困惑，尤其是简化程度和功能强弱的权衡（acjohnson55, esafak）。

争议焦点：
• RisingWave是否真的比其他工具（如Flink、Materialize）更简单易用，且能满足复杂需求。
• 在何种情况下应该选择RisingWave这样的系统，而不是使用传统的简单系统如Redis PubSub。

🌊 Ride the Wave of Streaming Data.

Benchmarks

Demos
RisingWave is a stream processing and management platform designed to offer the
simplest
and
most cost-effective
way to
process
,
analyze
, and
manage
real-time event data — with built-in support for the
Apache Iceberg™
open table format. It provides both a Postgres-compatible
SQL interface
and a DataFrame-style
Python interface
.
RisingWave can
ingest
millions of events per second, continuously
join and analyze
live streams with historical data,
serve
ad-hoc queries at low latency, and
persist
fresh, consistent results to Apache Iceberg™ or any other downstream system.
Try it out in 60 seconds
Install RisingWave standalone mode:
curl -L https://risingwave.com/sh
|
sh
To learn about other installation options, such as using a Docker image, see
Quick Start
.
Stream, Store, and Query — All in One
RisingWave delivers a full
end-to-end streaming data platform
— combining real-time processing with built-in storage and open-format persistence.
It supports:
Ingestion:
Ingest millions of events per second from streaming and batch sources.
Stream processing:
Perform real-time incremental processing to join and analyze live data with historical tables.
Delivery:
Deliver fresh, consistent results to data lakes (e.g., Apache Iceberg™) or any destination.
What sets RisingWave apart is its integrated storage engine:
Online serving:
Row-based storage optimized for point and range queries with single-digit millisecond latency.
Offline persistence:
Built-in Apache Iceberg™ integration for low-cost, durable storage with open access for external query engines.
With RisingWave, real-time data isn’t just processed — it’s stored, queried, and shared across your entire stack.
Key design decisions
RisingWave is designed to be easier to use and more cost-efficient:
PostgreSQL compatibility
Seamless integration:
Connects via the PostgreSQL wire protocol, working with psql, JDBC, and any Postgres tool.
Expressive SQL:
Supports structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data with a familiar SQL dialect.
No manual state tuning:
Eliminates complex state management configurations.
S3 as primary storage
RisingWave stores tables, materialized views, and internal states of stream processing jobs in S3 (or equivalent object storage), providing:
High performance:
Optimized for complex queries, including joins and time windowing.
Fast recovery:
Restores from system failures within seconds.
Dynamic scaling
:
Instantly adjusts resources to handle workload spikes.
Elastic disk cache
Beyond caching hot data in memory, RisingWave supports
elastic disk cache
, a powerful performance optimization that uses local disks or EBS for efficient data caching. This minimizes access to S3, lowering processing latency and cutting S3 access costs.
Apache Iceberg™ native support
RisingWave
natively integrates with Apache Iceberg™
, enabling continuous ingestion of streaming data into Iceberg tables. It can also read directly from Iceberg, perform automatic compaction, and maintain table health over time. Since Iceberg is an open table format, results are accessible by other query engines — making storage not only cost-efficient, but interoperable by design.
In what use cases does RisingWave excel?
RisingWave is particularly effective for the following use cases:
Streaming analytics
: Achieve sub-second data freshness in live dashboards, ideal for high-stakes scenarios like stock trading, sports betting, and IoT monitoring.
Event-driven applications
: Devel

data.title: A New Geometry for Einstein's Theory of Relativity
data.author: jandrewrogers
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了一组维也纳的数学家正在开发工具，以扩展爱因斯坦广义相对论的适用范围。传统相对论通过10个相互关联的微分方程描述物质和能量如何弯曲时空，但在遇到如黑洞中心奇点等非平滑几何情况时，这些方程失效。数学家Clemens Sämann和Michael Kunzinger试图找到不依赖平滑性和微分的新方法，以应对这些极端环境。他们与团队合作，重新推导了宇宙核心定理，并提出了一个新几何框架，能够处理更复杂和不规则的时空结构，旨在为相对论提供更坚实的数学基础。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对物理学理论（特别是广义相对论、奇点、振荡理论等）的不同理解和看法

不同观点：
• [cluckindan] 提出一种非严谨的振荡理论，认为一切存在都是振荡，这些振荡通过相互作用形成基本粒子，并最终产生质量和多维因果结构。该观点强调了我们作为系统内部观察者，无法直接体验非局部性，存在似乎是维度分离的。
  - 论据：振荡之间的共振与不谐导致高阶结构的形成，奇点中的结构崩溃会导致量子真空，进而释放无质量和非局部性的成分。

• [WCSTombs] 对文章表示赞赏，并联想到自己曾研究的关于将某些概念从平滑流形推广到"非平滑"环境的工作，特别是最优传输（optimal transport）的概念。
  - 论据：最优传输在纯数学和应用数学中未得到足够重视，本有可能成为其博士论文的主题，但由于人生选择未能继续探索。

• [Sniffnoy] 对新奇点定理的出现持怀疑态度，认为这可能不是积极的信号。根据其理解，奇点是广义相对论在极端尺度下由于缺乏量子引力理论而出现的非物理现象。
  - 争议焦点：奇点是否是真实的物理存在，还是仅仅是广义相对论在量子尺度下的缺陷表现。理想的理论应避免奇点。

• [ggdG] 质疑广义相对论是否确实告诉我们宇宙在膨胀，认为广义相对论的微分方程可以根据不同的初始条件和约束产生不同的解。
  - 论据：广义相对论本身只是提供了解决方案的框架，具体的解依赖于天文观测提供的条件和约束。

• [michaelsbradley] 提到可以用欧几里得度量来重新表述广义相对论，而非传统的闵可夫斯基度量，并提供了一个相关网站链接。
  - 补充：这种重新表述提供了一种不同的几何视角，可能对理解广义相对论有帮助。

• [kittikitti] 对文章持批评态度，认为其只是为尚未经过同行评审的理论做市场宣传，填补爱因斯坦粉丝的点击量需求。
  - 论据：希望这些数学家能够完善爱因斯坦的广义相对论，使其与现代物理学相容，而不是仅仅做一些表面文章。

补充讨论：
- 不同评论者对奇点和广义相对论的看法存在明显争议，一部分人认为奇点是理论缺陷的表现，另一部分人则探讨了广义相对论的不同数学表述及其物理意义。
- 对新理论的接受度和其在现代物理学中的应用前景也是讨论的重点，尤其是对新理论是否能经过实验验证并融入现有物理框架的关注。

A New Geometry for Einstein’s Theory of Relativity
By

A team of mathematicians based in Vienna is developing tools to extend the scope of general relativity.

I
n October 2015, a young mathematician named
Clemens Sämann
was flying home to Austria from a conference in Turin, Italy, when he had a chance encounter. He found himself seated beside
Michael Kunzinger
, another conference attendee. Kunzinger was a math professor at the University of Vienna, where Sämann had just started his postdoctoral research. They soon got to talking, landing on a subject Sämann had started thinking about in graduate school — whether there was a mathematical way to get around the limitations of Albert Einstein’s general theory of relativity.
Einstein’s theory defines gravity as the curvature of space-time caused by the presence of matter and energy. Since its formulation in 1915, it has held up remarkably well. Consisting of 10 interconnected differential equations, the theory describes how objects fall, how light bends, and how planets, stars and galaxies move. It tells us that the universe is expanding, and it predicted the existence of both black holes and gravitational waves a century before they were definitively observed.
But in spite of these successes, Einstein’s theory also has shortcomings. Its equations can only describe how matter curves space-time when the geometry of that space-time is smooth — with no sharp corners or cusps, no regions where it suddenly becomes jagged. Picture space-time as a flat rubber sheet, and matter as a bowling ball placed on that sheet, causing it to bend. If space-time is smooth, then this bending will be gradual.
But physicists know that’s not always true. A black hole, for instance, warps space-time more violently, causing the sheet to bend sharply until, at the black hole’s center (a so-called singularity), the curvature “blows up,” becoming infinite. Some physicists even posit that space-time doesn’t become non-smooth only at isolated singularities, but at every point. On the smallest scales, space-time might be “discrete,” or pixelated — broken up into tiny, disconnected bits in the same way that a fluid, while appearing to be a single uniform entity, is actually made up of distinct atoms and molecules.
In these situations, general relativity hits an impasse. Whenever space-time isn’t sufficiently smooth, Einstein’s equations stop working. They can no longer tell us how matter curves space-time, or how curved space-time influences matter.
That’s because the equations rely on a technique from calculus
called differentiation
that measures how quickly functions change, and differentiation is no longer possible in settings that are far from smooth. And so, on their flight back to Austria, Kunzinger and Sämann wondered whether they could devise alternative methods — ones that would still work in the inhospitable environments where the usual tools of calculus broke down.

Clemens Sämann has helped prove important singularity theorems in space-times that “could have corners, edges and folds.”
Der Knopfdrücker
The pair wouldn’t start working on the problem in earnest for another year. But since then, they’ve made significant advances toward their goal. They’ve found new ways to estimate curvature and other geometric properties without relying on smoothness and differentiation. In collaboration with other researchers, they’ve used their methods to rederive (and sometimes strengthen) core theorems about the universe without depending on Einstein’s equations, putting those theorems on even firmer mathematical footing.
And they’re now part of
an ambitious new program
— launched last year under the direction of
Roland Steinbauer
, another University of Vienna mathematician — that aims to provide “a new geometry for Einstein’s theory of relativity and beyond.”
“Standard general relativity talks about geometric objects, namely space-times, but only if they behave nicely enough,” Steinbauer said. “With this new framework, we can go beyond that. We can handle very edgy objects, very badly behaved objects.”
A Path Via Triangulation
When Kunzinger and Sämann started working together in 2016, their first goal was to revisit one of the most basic concepts to appear in Einstein’s equations: curvature.

  - 争议焦点：奇点是否是真实的物理存在，还是仅仅是广义相对论在量子尺度下的缺陷表现。理想的理论应避免奇点。

• [ggdG] 质疑广义相对论是否确实告诉我们宇宙在膨胀，认为广义相对论的微分方程可以根据不同的初始条件和约束产生不同的解。
  - 论据：广义相对论本身只是提供了解决方案的框架，具体的解依赖于天文观测提供的条件和约束。

• [michaelsbradley] 提到可以用欧几里得度量来重新表述广义相对论，而非传统的闵可夫斯基度量，并提供了一个相关网站链接。
  - 补充：这种重新表述提供了一种不同的几何视角，可能对理解广义相对论有帮助。

• [kittikitti] 对文章持批评态度，认为其只是为尚未经过同行评审的理论做市场宣传，填补爱因斯坦粉丝的点击量需求。
  - 论据：希望这些数学家能够完善爱因斯坦的广义相对论，使其与现代物理学相容，而不是仅仅做一些表面文章。

补充讨论：
- 不同评论者对奇点和广义相对论的看法存在明显争议，一部分人认为奇点是理论缺陷的表现，另一部分人则探讨了广义相对论的不同数学表述及其物理意义。
- 对新理论的接受度和其在现代物理学中的应用前景也是讨论的重点，尤其是对新理论是否能经过实验验证并融入现有物理框架的关注。

data.title: Replication of Quantum Factorisation Records with a VIC-20, an Abacus, and a Dog
data.author: teddyh
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种通过使用1981年的VIC-20 8位家用电脑、算盘和一只狗来实现和超越当前量子因数分解记录的实现方法。作者希望此工作能够激励未来在量子因数分解记录上的进一步尝试。文章包含对原文的一些小修订，以更正打字错误、澄清因数分解中sqrt(n)的用法，并添加了电子邮件地址。本文属于攻击与密码分析类别，并以预印本形式发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：量子计算、因子分解、图表错误、对量子计算进展的评价以及相关竞赛的讨论。

不同观点：
• [cbm-vic-20] 通过使用校准过的参考狗Scribble进行实验，验证了因子分解15和21的过程。然而，实验并不简单，因为Scribble很乖，几乎不叫。

• [brontitall] 认为图3中存在错误，指出无符号变量m总是 >= 0，导致while循环不会终止。

• [rahimnathwani] 提供了之前讨论的链接，并引用了一篇文章，指出“量子计算进展不能单凭能因子分解的最大数来衡量”，并引用Dan Bernstein的观点，认为如果量子计算遇到物理障碍，世界可能会变得更好。

• [tomgag] 分享了自己对整个事件的看法，支持rahimnathwani的观点，并提供了相关链接，进一步讨论量子计算的进展不应以能因子分解的最大数来衡量。

• [spr-alex] 提到qdayprize.org上的搜索空间太小，不足以成为一个有意义的竞赛，且规则未明确如何判断“量子性”的有效性。

• [mycall] 简单表达了对讨论的喜爱。

• [OhMeadhbh] 对Peter Gutmann的参与表示幽默回应。

• [hagbard_c] 以幽默方式描述了自己在研究弦理论时的情景，用食物和动物肢体类比弦理论的维度，增加了讨论的趣味性。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是量子计算进展的评价标准，部分评论者认为不能单凭因子分解能力来衡量。
• 另一个技术性问题是对图表中错误的指出和讨论，[brontitall] 指出了图3中的潜在错误。
• 对量子计算竞赛的有效性和规则也提出了质疑，特别是在如何判断量子性方面。

Abstract
This paper presents implementations that match and, where possible, exceed current quantum factorisation records using a VIC-20 8-bit home computer from 1981, an abacus, and a dog.  We hope that this work will inspire future efforts to match any further quantum factorisation records, should they arise.

data.title: Multiplatform Matrix Multiplication Kernels
data.author: homarp
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了现代计算中矩阵乘法的重要性及其在人工智能和深度学习中的核心作用。尽管NVIDIA通过Tensor Cores等技术大幅提升了矩阵乘法的速度，但预编译的矩阵乘法内核缺乏灵活性。当前的主要瓶颈在于数据移动，而非计算本身。为了优化性能，需减少数据移动，并将多个内核或算法融合成单个内核。NVIDIA的CUTLASS提供了定制矩阵乘法内核的工具，但仅支持NVIDIA GPU，限制了可移植性。为此，作者开发了CubeCL和矩阵乘法内核引擎，能够为任何GPU甚至CPU生成优化内核。文章还介绍了现代GPU的架构和执行粒度，强调了同步和内存访问优化对高性能计算的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Burn项目及其技术设计的讨论

不同观点：
• Archit3ch认为Metal支持非常有价值，但指出仅仅做矩阵乘法并不足够，还需要将其他操作融合进MatMul内核以提升性能，并质疑Burn开发者如何解决这一问题。
• Lerc对有缺陷的矩阵乘法进行了探讨，提出是否可以在正确性和性能之间找到平衡，从而节省计算量，尤其是在像梯度下降这样对少量错误值不敏感的算法中。
• Saagarjha认为Burn的API设计类似于CUTLASS，但对是否能通过API实现更复杂的操作（如自定义尾声和分块模式）表示怀疑。
• Nathanielsimard作为Burn的开发者之一，邀请大家提出问题和意见。
• Burnt-resistor回顾了GPU的发展历史，强调了快速浮点运算和图形处理的需求，以此背景讨论Burn项目。
• Raphaelty对Burn表示出尝试兴趣。
• Semessier曾经预测矩阵乘法会在专用硬件上实现，并对目前仍需使用GPU表示意外。
• Apitman提问是否可以在WebGPU中实现类似Burn的功能。
• Airstrike对Burn表示赞赏。
• Almostgotcaught对Burn项目中使用的术语命名提出批评，认为这些命名与现有的CUDA和Vulkan/WGPU命名不一致，增加了理解难度，并以NVIDIA和AMD的文档为例说明。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是Burn项目是否能有效融合其他操作以提升性能（Archit3ch的观点）。
• 另一个讨论点是对矩阵乘法中计算精度与性能的权衡（Lerc的观点）。
• 还有对API设计是否足够表达复杂操作的质疑（Saagarjha的观点）。
• 术语命名的不一致性引起了almostgotcaught的不满，认为这可能导致开发者困惑。
• 其他评论多为正面反馈或对项目表示兴趣。

sota-multiplatform-matmul
State-of-the-Art Multiplatform Matrix Multiplication Kernels
Fri, Jul 18, 2025
Louis Fortier-Dubois
Nathaniel Simard
Few algorithmic problems are as central to modern computing as matrix
multiplication. It is fundamental to AI, forming the basis of fully
connected layers used throughout neural networks. In transformer
architectures,
most of the computation
is spent performing matrix
multiplication. And since compute largely determines capability, faster
matrix multiplication algorithms directly translate into more powerful
models
[
1
]
.
NVIDIA probably deserves much of the credit for making matrix
multiplication fast. Their early focus on building GPUs for gaming
drove major improvements in general-purpose linear algebra. As deep
learning took over, they introduced Tensor Cores — specialized units
designed to accelerate matrix multiplication in AI models.
With hardware evolving to support these new workloads, accelerators
have become increasingly complex, and writing high-performance code
for them remains challenging. To ease this burden, hardware vendors
like NVIDIA, AMD and Intel provide off-the-shelf matrix multiplication
kernels, typically integrated into tensor libraries. However, the
quality and performance of these kernels vary. While NVIDIA’s
implementations, through libraries like cuBLAS
[
2
]
and cuDNN
[
3
]
, are highly optimized,
a key limitation remains: as precompiled binaries, they lack flexibility
and extensibility.
In modern AI workloads, the primary bottleneck is no longer
computation. It's data movement. Moving data from memory to registers
often costs more than performing the actual calculations. The best way
to optimize for this is quite obvious: minimize data movement. A
powerful way to achieve this is to fuse multiple kernels or algorithms
into a single kernel
[
4
]
. For
matrix multiplication, it means executing element-wise operations on
the values calculated
just before
writing them to global memory.
Pre-built matrix multiplication kernels don't support this kind of composition,
making custom kernel implementations necessary.
This is why NVIDIA created CUTLASS
[
5
]
: a set of C++ templates that help developers tailor
matrix-multiplication kernels to their needs. However, it remains very
intricate to use and, of course, only works on NVIDIA GPUs.
As a result, using CUTLASS to optimize a model often comes at the cost
of portability. But wouldn't it be better to optimize models across
platforms? That’s why we built CubeCL
[
6
]
, and on top of it, a matrix multiplication kernel engine
[
7
]
that searches for and generates optimized kernels for any GPU and even
CPUs.
Not Just an Algorithm
One of the main challenges with matrix multiplication is that the
input shapes strongly influence which algorithm performs best. As a
result, no single algorithm is optimal in all cases; different shapes
require different strategies.
To address this, we built an engine that actually makes it very easy
to create different algorithms that are totally configurable. At its
core is a multi-level matrix multiplication architecture that we'll
explore in this blog.
...Or, skip the theory and
jump straight to benchmarks
.
A Bit on the Hardware First
Before diving into the solution, let's briefly review the architecture
of modern GPUs. A GPU consists of multiple streaming multiprocessors
(SMs), each capable of independently executing parts of a program in
parallel. Each SM has a fixed set of resources shared across multiple
concurrent executions.
There are three main levels of execution granularity:
Unit
(
thread
in CUDA,
invocation
in Vulkan/Wgpu):
the smallest execution entity performing computations.
Plane
(
warp
in CUDA,
subgroup
in Vulkan/Wgpu): a
group of (typically 32) units executing in lockstep and able to share
data efficiently through registers.
Cube
(
thread block
in CUDA,
workgroup
in Vulkan/Wgpu):
a group of units that execute on the same SM, sharing memory and able
to synchronize.
Grasping the concept of planes can be challenging when first
programming GPUs, because it’s extremely implicit. One of the GPU's
parallel axes is actually more efficient when executed in sync, but
this is generally not reflected in the code. Units within the same
plane perform more efficiently when they execute the same instruction
simultaneously, whereas branching is more acceptable between different
planes. Additionally, data access is faster when each unit, in turn,
loads from consecutive addresses, allowing a single instruction to
fetch a contiguous block of memory. This is known as
coalesced memory access
and is central to most memory optimizations. As a result, many high-performance
computing kernels treat the plane—not the individual unit—as the smallest
computation primitive, in order to avoid branching and maximize performance.

data.title: Broadcom to discontinue free Bitnami Helm charts
data.author: mmoogle
data.article_summary:
文章主要介绍了Bitnami目录即将于2025年8月28日进行的变化。主要包括：

1. **社区目录**：禁用Debian系镜像生成，现有镜像将移至Bitnami Legacy仓库，不再更新。
2. **Bitnami Secure Images**：推出更安全、加固的企业级镜像，提供长期支持和安全补丁，但需要订阅。
3. **迁移时间表**：
   - 现在至2025年8月28日：发布弃用通知，用户需更新CI/CD管道和镜像引用。
   - 2025年8月28日：公共目录转为社区版精简镜像，旧版镜像移至Bitnami Legacy仓库。
   - 2025年8月28日后：社区用户只能使用最新的“latest”标签镜像，生产环境用户需订阅Secure Images以获取支持和安全更新。

Bitnami将继续在GitHub上维护开源代码，并提供免费社区版镜像，但完整支持和版本历史需通过订阅获取。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Bitnami容器镜像迁移及其影响

不同观点：
• **KronisLV的观点**：KronisLV对Bitnami容器镜像迁移表示不满，因为他们曾依赖Bitnami镜像，包括Apache2、MariaDB、Redis、MongoDB等。他们现在需要迁移到上游镜像或自行构建，并表示会尽量避免使用与Broadcom相关的产品。同时，他们提到Bitnami的代码仍在GitHub上维护，但对实际操作表示困惑。

• **ridruejo的观点**：作为Bitnami的联合创始人，ridruejo对这项商业决定感到不解，但对Bitnami的技术团队仍持肯定态度。

• **chuckadams的观点**：chuckadams用讽刺的语气暗示Broadcom的决策风格一贯如此，不必大惊小怪。

• **remram的观点**：remram对公告的时间和执行细节感到困惑，特别是关于镜像何时从docker.io/bitnami迁移到bitnamilegacy的具体时间，以及用户需要采取的行动。

• **janjongboom的观点**：janjongboom担心此次迁移会破坏依赖Bitnami镜像的系统，并提到他们曾参与创建的stablebuild.com项目，旨在解决此类问题。

• **dpkirchner的观点**：dpkirchner表示可能会因此放弃使用Helm charts，并正在考虑其他替代方案。

• **Youden的观点**：Youden指出，尽管镜像的二进制形式不再更新，但其源代码仍在GitHub上维护，可能会有社区支持的二进制构建出现。

• **ntqz的观点**：ntqz表示早已预料到这种情况，并正在考虑将代码库从Spring迁移到其他框架如Quarkus、Helidon等。

• **sseveran的观点**：sseveran关注Bitnami charts的替代方案问题。

• **moorow的观点**：moorow提到Bitnami镜像在安全方面存在问题，例如最近的CVE 9.4漏洞，影响了大量云主机。

• **sbstp的观点**：sbstp担心RabbitMQ是否会受到影响。

📢 Overview
As of August 28th, 2025, the Bitnami public catalog will undergo the following changes:
Community catalog
Disable images generation for Debian-based images and gradually move existing ones to a
Bitnami Legacy
repository
.
A focused set of more hardened, more secure images. These free images are intended for development and are only available on the “latest” tag. You can find them at
https://hub.docker.com/u/bitnamisecure
.
Helm charts and container images' open-source code will continue to be maintained up-to-date and accessible on GitHub under the Apache 2 license.
Bitnami Secure Images
Production-ready, enterprise-grade containers and Helm charts will move under the Bitnami Secure Images offering.
Benefits include:
Hardened, low-attack-surface operating system
Continuous rebuilds with the latest security patches (SLSA Level 3)
Industry-standard CVE transparency (VEX, KEV)
SBOMs and compliance artifacts
Enterprise support and LTS branches
Access to the entire catalog of applications (over 280)
Minimal distroless runtime images
Legacy repository migration
All existing container images, including older or versioned tags (e.g.,
2.50.0
,
10.6
), will be moved from the public catalog (
docker.io/bitnami
) to the
Bitnami Legacy
repository
(
docker.io/bitnamilegacy
). This legacy catalog will receive no further updates or support and should only be used for temporary migration purposes.
Suppose your deployed Helm chart is failing to pull images from
docker.io/bitnami
. In that case, you can resolve this by subscribing to Bitnami Secure Images, ensuring that the Helm charts receive continued support and security updates. As a temporary workaround, you can upgrade to the same version and update the repository parameter for each container image to the
Bitnami Legacy
repository
.
🗓️ Timeline
Now – August 28th, 2025
You will see deprecation notices in READMEs and documentation.
Plan your migration: Update CI/CD pipelines, Helm repos, and image references.
Start trying out the new hardened images available to the community today at
https://hub.docker.com/u/bitnamisecure
.
August 28th, 2025
The
public catalog
switches to the limited community-tier subset of container images (the same images that are initially available here at
https://hub.docker.com/u/bitnamisecure
).
Legacy assets are archived in the
Bitnami Legacy
repository
.
Post-August 28th, 2025
For development purposes, community-tier users are restricted to pulling only the most recent ‘latest’ tags of the limited community-tier subset of container images.
Production users should subscribe to Bitnami Secure Images for full version support at
https://www.arrow.com/globalecs/uk/products/bitnami-secure-images/#CTA
.
FAQ
Q: What is the
Bitnami Legacy
repository
?
A:
The
Bitnami Legacy
repository
is an archive that will host all older container images, including versioned tags (e.g.,
2.50.0
,
10.6
) that are no longer maintained in the main Bitnami catalog. These images will not receive updates, fixes, or support and should only be used as a temporary fallback for migration purposes. Even though there are no updates to the container images, the Bitnami project continues to make its source available at
bitnami/containers
under the Apache 2 license.
Q: How is
Bitnami Legacy
repository
different than
Bitnami Mainline
repository
?
A:
The
Bitnami Mainline
repository
(
docker.io/bitnami
) currently hosts regularly updated and supported container images, including free and enterprise-grade offerings.
The
Bitnami Legacy
repository
will contain archived versions that will no longer receive updates. It is provided solely to help with migration during the transition.
After August 28th, 2025, only a limited set of hardened images will remain in the
Bitnami Mainline
repository
. All others will be moved to the
Bitnami Legacy
repository
.

Bitnami Mainline
repository
need to do before August 28th, 2025?
A:
Users should:
Review and update CI/CD pipelines to avoid relying on deprecated images.
Consider subscribing to Bitnami Secure Images if they need continued support, security updates, or access to full version history at
https://www.arrow.com/globalecs/uk/products/bitnami-secure-images/#CTA
.
Upgrade their deployments
If the deployed application belongs to the limited set of hardened images available under the new free community tier, double-check check the used tags are still updated.
Otherwise, point to the
Bitnami Legacy
repository
as a temporary workaround.

data.title: Benben: An audio player for the terminal, written in Common Lisp
data.author: trocado
data.article_summary: Benben是一款适用于Linux及类似Unix系统的命令行音频播放器和转换器，具有复古风格界面，特别适合习惯在终端操作的用户。它支持多种音频格式，能够高效播放和转换文件，并具备多线程用户界面、播放列表循环、远程控制等功能。最新版本为v0.6.1，开发者Remilia Scarlet正在用Common Lisp重写程序。用户可以通过命令行操作播放、转换音频文件，支持ReplayGain、VU表、EQ等效果。Benben是开源软件，采用GNU Affero General Public License v3许可。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：某软件的当前和未来版本的技术细节、使用体验、功能支持情况以及与其他软件的对比。

不同观点：
• [shawn_w] 指出，根据细节信息，该软件的下一重要版本将使用Common Lisp编写，但目前的版本是用Crystal编写的。
• [vindarel] 赞同该软件的当前实用性，强调了使用AppImage在Linux系统上简便的三步使用体验，并对Common Lisp在音频解码上的表现表示赞赏，指出其无需依赖绑定库。
• [superdisk] 也提到之前使用该软件的经历，确认其曾经用Crystal编写，并称赞其在处理VGM文件时的便捷和快速，同时表扬了开发者的响应速度和支持。
• [wtn] 指出该软件的开发者似乎没有计划支持MPEG-4音频文件，暗示了对某些功能缺失的不满。
• [user3939382] 提到了另一款软件cmus，并认为其在终端用户界面（TUI）中的表现优于iTunes，特别是在浏览音轨方面。

补充讨论：
• [moonlion_eth] 以幽默的方式表达了对Common Lisp的偏爱，暗示其在某些技术场景中的独特优势。

争议焦点：
• 软件未来版本从Crystal转向Common Lisp的技术选择，以及对MPEG-4音频文件支持的缺乏，可能是引发讨论者关注和不同意见的主要争议点。

总结：讨论围绕软件的技术实现、用户体验、功能支持以及与其他软件的对比展开，涉及对编程语言选择、功能需求和开发者响应的评价。

Benben
Benben
Benben is a fast and efficient command line audio player and audio converter for
Linux and other Unix-like systems with an oldschool-inspired interface.  It
supports multiple formats, and is especially suited to people who organize their
music in folders, and for those who prefer to use terminals instead of GUIs.
Starting with v0.7.0, it is written almost entirely in the
Common
Lisp
programming language.
The latest release is v0.6.1, released on December 22nd, 2024.
Releases, downloads, and AppImages for x86-64 Linux
Build from source
Full manual
(also in
in PDF format
)
Project Goals
FAQ page
Official Matrix channel
Benben is entirely written and maintained by one person, Remilia Scarlet!  If
you want to support her and Benben, you can
buy her a coffee on
Ko-Fi
, or support her through Liberapay.  Support
is greatly appreciated for this volunteer effort ^_^
Example Videos
Partition 36 - Overdrive
(Opus)
ZUN - 亡き王女の為のセプテット (Septette for a Dead Princess)
(MP3)
Partition 36 - Searching for My Identity
(Ogg Vorbis)
Skaven - Ice Frontier (Remix by Necros)
(Module/S3M)
SoulCalibur - Wings of Faith (Sophitia)
(VGM - Namco C352)
Partition 36 - The Mainframe
(FLAC)
Warcraft 2 - Human 2
(General MIDI)
The Partition 36 videos are songs written by Remilia.  Check out her
Bandcamp
page.
Supported Input Formats
VGM
Uncompressed (.vgm)
GZip compressed (.vgz)
ZStandard compressed (.vgzst)
BZip2 compressed (.vgb)
MPEG-1
MPEG-1 Layer III (.mp3)
MPEG-1 Layer II (.mp1)
MPEG-1 Layer I (.mp1)
Ogg Vorbis
Opus
FLAC
General MIDI (.mid)
MUS (.mus)
All module formats supported by
libxmp
Commodore 64 SID (.sid)
RIFF WAVE (.wav)
QOA
, the Quite OK Audio format
XQAF
, the Extended Quite OK Audio Format
WavPack
Sun Au (.au)
Notable Features
ALSA,
libout123
, and libao backends.
High-performance playback.
Fast, multi-threaded UI via
S-Lang
.
Multiple files can be specified and they will play one after the other.
Song and playlist looping.
Output audio over TCP.
Support for
XSPF and JSPF
playlists.
High quality resampling.
A powerful
Configuration file
support,
including support for per-song configurations.
Rendering (converting) multiple files in parallel to WAV or
Au
, with support for multiple
bit depths and sample rates, and both integer and floating point.
Optional effects:
Soft clipping with configurable oversampling.
Parametric EQ with an arbitrary number of bands.
Stereo enhancement effect.
Reverb with selectable type and preset.
DC offset filter.
Customizable VU meter.
Keyboard control support.
ReplayGain/RVA support.
Controllable remotely over a dedicated socket.
ListenBrainz support.
Command Line Examples
Below are various examples of how to use Benben.  Keep in mind that Benben is a
command line program, and does
NOT
have a file browser
by design
.  You
pass the files/directories you want to listen to in on the command line.
# Play an MP3 file and stop after it finishes
$ benben "Cool Song.mp3"
# Play a VGM and loop twice
$ benben --loop 2 "Another Cool Song.vgz"
# Play a directory of music.
$ benben /path/to/my-cool-album/
# Render (convert) multiple files files to WAVs in parallel, storing them in
# the current directory
$ benben --render *.ogg *.mp3
# Play various files and stop after it finishes
$ benben "Cool Song.vgz" spacedeb.mod "02 - E1M1.flac"
# Show the help information
$ benben --help
# Show version information
$ benben --version
# List reverb presets for "MVerb"
$ benben --reverb-type mverb --reverb-preset list
Development
Development Milestones
are listed in the wiki.
Version v0.7.0 is currently in development; the entire program and all of its
support libraries are being rewritten in Common Lisp.  Previous versions were
written in the
Crystal
programming language.  See
this post
and
this
post
for more information.
How do I contribute?
Go to
https://chiselapp.com/user/MistressRemilia/repository/benben
and clone the Fossil repository.
Create a new branch for your feature.
Push locally to the new branch.
Create a
bundle
with Fossil
that contains your changes.
Get in contact with Remilia via email, Fediverse, or open a ticket.
Contributors
Remilia Scarlet - creator and maintainer
Homepage:
https://remilia.sdf.org/
Fediverse:
@remilia@nanako-さめ.mooo.com
Email: zremiliaz@postzeoz.jpz  My real address does not contain Z's
Links and Licenses
Benben is under the
GNU Affero General Public License version
3

data.title: Third patient dies from acute liver failure caused by a Sarepta gene therapy
data.author: randycupertino
data.article_summary: 2025年7月17日，Sarepta Therapeutics公司宣布，一名51岁的患者在参与该公司针对2E型肢带肌营养不良症（Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy Type 2E）的基因疗法（SRP-9004）一期临床试验中死亡。这是该公司基因疗法导致的第三起死亡案例，死因与之前两例一样，均为急性肝毒性。此前，Sarepta的Duchenne肌营养不良症基因疗法Elevidys也曾引发类似问题。公司发言人Tracy Sorrentino证实了这一事件。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Sarepta基因治疗药物的效果、技术选择、政策监管及其经济影响

不同观点：
• **关于技术和选择的讨论：**
  - [sampl3username] 提出疑问，为什么Sarepta选择使用腺相关病毒（AAV）作为基因传递载体，而不是脂质纳米颗粒。这可能表明对AAV载体安全性和有效性的担忧，以及对不同技术路线的比较。
  - [snitty] 指出基因治疗面临的挑战，尤其是人体对基因治疗的防御机制，暗示这些治疗需要克服复杂的生物障碍，可能隐含对AAV等技术的质疑。

• **关于政策和责任的讨论：**
  - [csours] 强调无论社会做出什么决策或政策，都会随着时间改变，尤其是当人们感到无法获得所需治疗时。该评论指出，将责任归咎于FDA（美国食品药品监督管理局）很容易，但更理想的方式是共同承担责任和保持谦逊。这反映出对政策灵活性和社会责任的关注。

• **关于经济影响的讨论：**
  - [OsrsNeedsf2P] 提到Sarepta的股票在过去6个月内下跌了90%，当天跌幅达37%，表明对该公司经济状况的担忧。
  - [gary_0] 指出该治疗费用高达320万美元，可能在经济上引发对该疗法是否可行和合理的讨论。

• **关于疗效和潜力的讨论：**
  - [simmerup] 感叹基因疗法非常有前景，尽管当前可能面临问题，但依然对其未来充满希望。
  - [forgotpwagain] 提供了一个关于基因疗法未达预期的讨论链接，暗示对基因疗法整体发展的反思和质疑。

补充讨论：
• **信息获取的困难：**
  - [fsckboy] 抱怨付费墙阻碍了对相关新闻的阅读，并提到股票价格当天下跌了40%。同时，也对疗法的"效益"提出疑问，即在多大程度上该疗法是"值得的"。这表明了对信息透明度和疗效评估的需求。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于Sarepta选择的AAV载体技术的合理性、基因治疗在人体中的有效性及其高昂的治疗费用是否能带来相应的效益。同时，政策监管的灵活性和社会责任的分担也是讨论中的潜在争议点。

data.title: Making a StringBuffer in C, and questioning my sanity
data.author: coneonthefloor
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是一位开发者在用C语言编写代码时的心得与经验分享。作者自嘲在使用C语言时质疑自己的编程能力，认为C语言不易使用，但对使用它感到享受，尤其是在没有 deadline 或业务关键软件需要交付时。作者还分享了一个自己实现的动态字符串缓冲区（StringBuffer）代码，包括初始化、操作（如追加、预置、删除、替换）、搜索与分割以及清理内存等功能。作者特别提到 "replace" 和 "remove" 功能的实现较为复杂，需要仔细处理内存管理。最后提供了代码的GitHub链接供参考。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：字符串和缓冲区实现的效率、设计选择、代码风格以及是否应继续使用C语言

不同观点：
• [o11c] 认为当前实现对于按值传递类型不友好，导致了不必要的分配开销。同时，该实现优先考虑可变性，并提供了一些低效的操作。o11c 还指出，大多数字符串实现的常见问题是只提供单一类型，而没有提供一系列可以在不同场景中使用的兼容类型，这些类型在所有权、生命周期和表示等方面有所不同。

• [WalterBright] 提出了一种优化建议，即将容量增加的倍数从2改为1.5，以提高性能，并提供了一个相关的Stack Overflow链接作为参考。

• [kazinator] 指出了当前代码中的一个潜在无限循环问题，并详细分析了原因：由于使用了无符号类型（size_t），当所需容量达到size_t的最大值（SIZE_MAX）时，容量翻倍的操作会导致循环无法终止。

• [burnt-resistor] 建议重构代码，创建一个包含void* buf、size_t capacity和size_t refcount的基本缓冲区，然后使用写时复制（CoW）逻辑实现字符串操作。这样可以使子字符串的只读引用变得廉价，并在修改时进行复制或重新分配。

• [teo_zero] 对函数参数中混合使用StringBuffer和C字符串表示不满，认为这样容易引起混淆，并建议统一使用StringBuffer类型作为参数。

• [gblargg] 指出代码中错误处理的不一致性，一些函数有错误报告机制（如返回NULL），而其他函数却没有，这可能导致调试困难。

• [ranger_danger] 提供了一个外部参考项目（sds），可能对解决当前问题有帮助。

• [p0w3n3d] 提出了一种对C语言的扩展建议，包括命名空间和类语法糖，以简化C语言中的面向对象编程，但这一建议被[improgrammer007]反对。

• [improgrammer007] 认为不应在C中重新发明轮子，建议直接使用C++，因为C++在性能关键的情况下提供了更多现成的功能，而在现代编程中继续使用C语言的理由应该很少。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是字符串实现的设计选择和优化方法，包括容量增长倍数的选择和潜在的无限循环问题。
• 另一个焦点是代码风格和参数类型的一致性，[teo_zero]和[gblargg]都对代码中的不一致性提出了批评。
• 最后，关于是否应继续使用C语言以及是否应引入新的语言特性，也存在一定的争议。

data.title: Section 174 is reversed, mostly
data.author: jawns
data.article_summary:
《The Pragmatic Engineer》报道，美国税法第174条对科技公司的影响有所缓解，但并非完全取消。2017年引入的第174条在2022年生效，导致科技公司在2023年面临开发人员薪资无法当年全额抵扣的问题，需分5年（美国内）或15年（美国外）摊销，对小型企业和盈利微薄的公司影响尤为严重。

好消息是，新法案撤销了针对美国内员工的限制，企业可选择当年全额抵扣开发人员薪资，且可追溯至2022年，允许重新申报退税。然而，针对美国外开发人员的薪资仍需15年摊销，可能促使美国科技公司减少海外招聘。整体而言，这一变化对美国内企业有利，但对海外开发人员可能不利。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Section 174修订对美国软件工程师薪资和就业市场的影响

不同观点：
• [g42gregory] 认为谷歌等大公司有能力影响政府决策，因此质疑单凭立法就能对公司底线产生如此大影响。他怀疑此事背后是否有更多未披露的细节。
• [avbanks] 认为Section 174的影响被低估了，并将其与近期的裁员潮联系起来，暗示该法律可能是裁员的直接原因。
• [breakyerself] 以讽刺的语气批评政府在处理此事上的失误，暗示政府通常只会把事情搞砸，而这次似乎打破了这一惯例。
• [vineyardmike] 认为该法律的修订对外包海外工作的成本增加有影响，可能有利于美国科技行业，并提出低生活成本或远程工作的美国员工可能受益，同时关注对其他行业的影响。
• [mertleee] 担心此“胜利”可能导致H1b签证上限增加，暗示可能出现更多外籍员工涌入美国市场。
• [throwawaybbq1] 希望撤销该法律能够逆转当前市场的低迷，并期待美国科技公司会因此增加招聘。
• [iooi] 质疑Section 174对FAANG公司是否真的有显著影响，认为小企业受影响更大。
• [qkeast] 关注15年摊销期是否仅适用于开发人员，询问设计师和产品经理等角色是否也受影响。
• [froggertoaster] 不理解为何15年摊销期会成为问题，暗示对该规定的反对意见可能站不住脚。
• [kevmo314] 对公司在亏损时选择摊销薪资的做法表示好奇，认为可能存在特定情况下选择摊销是有利的。
• [mlsu] 对Section 174的出台动机表示困惑，猜测可能与2022年硅谷高薪引发的不满有关，或有更深层次的政策原因。
• [spwa4] 批评政府每次增加税收时总是针对个人，而不是直接针对公司，并通过数学计算说明美国与非美国软件工程师的成本差距，认为该法律无法有效阻止工作岗位外流。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到外包和海外工作岗位的成本变化，以及该法律对美国与非美国员工的相对影响，反映出对全球化就业市场的关注。
• 一些评论（如[mertleee]和[spwa4]）提到了对H1b签证和外国开发人员的潜在影响，暗示法律修订可能带来意想不到的后果。
• 争议的焦点之一在于Section 174的影响是否被夸大，以及大公司是否真的无法通过政治手段避免此类立法的影响（如[g42gregory]和[iooi]的观点）。
• 部分评论对未来就业市场和公司决策的变化持观望态度，尤其是对大科技公司是否会因此改变招聘策略表示关注（如[throwawaybbq1]和[vineyardmike]）。

Finally, relief: tax regulation hurting the US tech industry is striked off for good - for the most part, that is.

Hi, this is Gergely with a bonus, free issue of the Pragmatic Engineer Newsletter. In every issue, I cover Big Tech and startups through the lens of senior engineers and engineering leaders. Today, we get into one out of four topics from
last week’s The Pulse
issue, which full subscribers received seven days ago. If you’ve been forwarded this email, you can
subscribe here
.
Since early 2024, a tax change in the US named “Section 174” has been plaguing tech companies in the country. It was introduced during the first Trump administration in 2017, came into effect in 2022, and impacted businesses from the tax year of 2023. The next year, many tech companies discovered just how bad S174 is.
In short, salaries paid to software engineers can no longer be deducted as a cost, like all other employee wages are. Instead, they must be amortized over 5 years for developers in the US, and for 15 years (for developers outside the US.) This treats software development similar to physical assets like servers. The big difference is that software is
not
an asset that necessarily has re-sale value.
We published a deepdive
on why this regulation was likely to result in more developers being fired by tech companies, and fewer being hired. The regulation especially hurt small businesses, bootstrapped companies, and those making a small loss or profit. In short, a small, bootstrapped company spending $1M in developer costs that made zero profits would have suddenly owed $189K in corporate tax thanks to this tax change:
The impact of Section 174 changes on a company that has $1M in revenue and $1M in labor costs. From
The Pulse: Will US companies hire fewer engineers due to Section 174?
The regulation was designed to increase tax revenue from tech companies and entered the tax code, applying to all software developers, except those in the oil and gas sectors! Due to Section 174, the US became the only country in the world where developer salaries cannot be expensed in the same tax year.
Read more in our deepdive on S174.
But things have changed. Some great news is that part of S174 is struck off , fully for US employees.
Buried deep
inside Trump’s “Big, Beautiful Bill”
is a provision that allows companies to keep deducting expenses related to software development in the same tax year. Basically, developer salaries can be deducted just like before 2023. Companies have the
choice
to amortize salaries if they want.
In the original draft, this was planned to be a temporary relief until 2030. But in the final bill it was removed permanently.
Additional good news is that costs can be expensed retroactively.
Also added in the bill is how companies can do two years of “catch-up:” businesses can re-file tax returns using the
old
expensing rules 2022-2024. Basically, companies hurt by having to pay more tax in 2022 to 2024 can go back and claim back the surplus they paid.
This is an immediate relief to all US companies, but it’s not all good.
The remaining thing that stings for companies is how foreign devs still need to be amortized for 15 years.
US companies making foreign software development-related expenditures like hiring staff, or paying for contracts abroad, are still mandated to be expensed over 15 years. This period is very long, and will incentivize US companies to consider cutting developers abroad, or recruiting less from outside the US.
US tech companies have done plenty of hiring abroad, especially in Europe and India. The regulation makes it clear that anything considered research and experimental (R&E) that’s done outside the US
needs
to be expensed over 15 years.
I expect US companies to hire more in the US, and less outside of it.
The updated Section 174 very clearly incentivises doing so. If you’re in the US: this is great news! If you’re outside, prepare for US-based companies to be incentivized to make cuts abroad, and to hire less outside of the US.

last week’s The Pulse
and
this week’s The Pulse
for more, timely analysis on the tech industry.

• [kevmo314] 对公司在亏损时选择摊销薪资的做法表示好奇，认为可能存在特定情况下选择摊销是有利的。
• [mlsu] 对Section 174的出台动机表示困惑，猜测可能与2022年硅谷高薪引发的不满有关，或有更深层次的政策原因。
• [spwa4] 批评政府每次增加税收时总是针对个人，而不是直接针对公司，并通过数学计算说明美国与非美国软件工程师的成本差距，认为该法律无法有效阻止工作岗位外流。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到外包和海外工作岗位的成本变化，以及该法律对美国与非美国员工的相对影响，反映出对全球化就业市场的关注。
• 一些评论（如[mertleee]和[spwa4]）提到了对H1b签证和外国开发人员的潜在影响，暗示法律修订可能带来意想不到的后果。
• 争议的焦点之一在于Section 174的影响是否被夸大，以及大公司是否真的无法通过政治手段避免此类立法的影响（如[g42gregory]和[iooi]的观点）。
• 部分评论对未来就业市场和公司决策的变化持观望态度，尤其是对大科技公司是否会因此改变招聘策略表示关注（如[throwawaybbq1]和[vineyardmike]）。

data.title: How to write Rust in the Linux kernel: part 3
data.author: chmaynard
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在Linux内核中使用Rust编程的接口和内存分配方法。Rust代码通过外部函数接口（FFI）调用C函数，但由于两者在内存释放和锁定方面的差异，直接调用内核C函数存在问题。为解决此问题，内核为Rust提供了集中化的绑定接口，以便统一和标准化，同时确保安全和质量。内存分配方面，Rust在内核中使用`kernel::alloc`模块，提供类似于C的`kmalloc`、`vmalloc`和`kvmallo`等分配方式，并支持指定分配标志和处理失败情况。Rust的内存分配器实现了`Allocator`接口，支持创建如`KBox`和`VVec`等结构，并允许使用`Arc`进行引用计数分配。内存分配时，程序员需根据具体需求选择合适的分配器和标志。

How to write Rust in the kernel: part 3
[LWN subscriber-only content]
Welcome to LWN.net
The following subscription-only content has been made available to you
by an LWN subscriber.  Thousands of subscribers depend on LWN for the
best news from the Linux and free software communities.  If you enjoy this
article, please consider
subscribing to LWN
.  Thank you
for visiting LWN.net!
By
Daroc Alden
July 18, 2025
Rust in the kernel
The interfaces between C and Rust in the kernel have grown over time; any
non-trivial Rust driver will use a number of these. Tasks like allocating memory,
dealing with immovable structures, and interacting with locks are necessary for
handling most devices. There are also many subsystem-specific bindings, but the
focus of this third item in our series on writing Rust in the kernel
will be on an overview of the bindings that all kernel Rust code
can be expected to use.
Rust code can call C using the
foreign function interface
(FFI); given that, one
potential way to integrate Rust into the kernel would have been to let Rust
code call kernel C functions directly. There are a few problems with that
approach, however:
__always_inline
functions, non-idiomatic APIs, etc.
In particular, C and Rust have different approaches to freeing memory and
locking.
During the early planning phases, the project
proposed
adopting a rule that there should be a
single, centralized set of Rust bindings for each subsystem,
as explained in
the kernel documentation
. This has
the disadvantage (compared to direct use of Rust's FFI)
of creating some extra work for a Rust programmer who wishes to
call into a new area of the kernel, but as more bindings are written that need
should go away over time. The advantage of the approach is that there's a single
set of standardized Rust interfaces to learn, with all of the documentation in
one
place
, which should make building and understanding the bindings less work
overall. The interfaces can also be reviewed by the Rust maintainers in one
place for safety and quality.
Allocating memory
Like C, Rust puts local variables (including compound structures)
on the stack by default. But most programs will
eventually need the flexibility offered by heap allocation and the limitations
on kernel-stack size mean that even purely local data may require
heap-allocation. In user space, Rust
programs use automatic heap allocations for some types — mainly
Box
(a smart pointer into the heap) and
Vec
(a growable, heap-allocated
array). In the kernel, these interfaces would not provide nearly enough control.
Instead, allocations are performed using the interfaces in the
kernel::alloc
module, which allow for specifying allocation flags
and handling the possibility of failure.
The Rust interfaces support three ways to allocate kernel memory:
Kmalloc
,
Vmalloc
, and
KVmalloc
, corresponding to the
memory-management API functions
with similar names.
The first two allocate physically contiguous memory
or virtually contiguous memory, respectively.
KVmalloc
first tries to allocate
physically contiguous memory, and then falls back to virtually contiguous memory. No matter which
allocator is used, the pointers that are exposed to Rust are part of the virtual
address space, as in C.
These three different types all implement the
Allocator
interface, which is similar to
the unstable user-space trait
of the same name. While the allocators can be used to directly create a
[u8]
(a sized array of bytes; conceptually similar to how
malloc()
returns a
void *
instead of a specific type),
the more ergonomic and less
error-prone use is to allocate
Box
or
Vec
structures. Since memory allocation is so common, the interfaces provide short
aliases for boxes and vectors made with each allocator, such as
KBox
,
KVBox
,
VVec
, etc. Reference counted allocations can be made
with
Arc
.
The choice of allocator is far from the only thing that kernel programmers care
about when allocating memory, however. Depending on the context, it may or may
not be acceptable to block, to swap, or to receive memory from
a particular zone
. When allocating, the flags in
kernel::alloc::flags
can be used to
specify more details
about how the necessary memory should be obtained:
let boxed_integer: Result<KBox<u64>, AllocError> = KBox::new(42, GFP_KERNEL);
That example allocates an unsigned 64-bit integer, initialized to 42, with the
usual set of allocation flags (
GFP_KERNEL
).
For a small allocation like this, that likely means the
memory will come from the kernel's slab allocator, possibly after triggering
memory reclamation or blocking.
This particular allocation
cannot fail
, but a larger one using the same API could,
if there is no suitable memory available,
even after reclamation.

data.title: Ccusage: A CLI tool for analyzing Claude Code usage from local JSONL files
data.author: kristianp
data.article_summary: **ccusage** 是一个用于分析本地 JSONL 文件中 Claude 代码使用情况的 CLI 工具。它能够快速生成每日、每月和会话级别的报告，显示 token 使用量和费用，支持实时监控和按模型 breakdown 的成本分析。该工具提供多种命令和选项，如日期过滤、JSON 输出和自定义路径等，且具有小巧的 bundle 体积和美观的输出格式。支持离线模式和 MCP 集成，便于与其它工具结合使用。安装可选，推荐使用 **bunx** 运行以获得最佳速度。文档和更多信息可访问 [ccusage.com](ccusage.com)。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Anthropic的API定价、性能、安全性等方面的看法和讨论。

不同观点：
• [关于定价和成本] extr认为Anthropic的API（如Sonnet和Opus）定价过高，尤其是与提供的服务成本相比。他以自己使用$100/mo的Max计划但产生$600-800/mo的费用为例，质疑Anthropic的利润空间，并提到Sonnet和Opus的价格高得离谱。不过，他也表示对Anthropic整体持乐观态度，认为他们在指令执行、可靠性和可预测性方面表现出色，具有独特的"心智理论"。

• [关于性能和性价比] extr指出，虽然Sonnet和Opus在纯编码任务上不如O3/Grok4，且不像Kimi K2那样具有性价比，但它们在指令执行和可靠性方面表现出色，有其独特的优势。

• [关于安全性] thebestmoshe对使用bunx、pnpx、npx等工具运行代码的安全性表示担忧，认为让用户习惯于运行这类具有系统完全访问权限的代码可能带来安全隐患。不过，他也提到这与安装npm包没有本质区别。

补充讨论：
• extr对Anthropic是否会像Cursor一样面临困境表示关注，但认为Anthropic有能力通过优化推理成本避免类似问题。
• thebestmoshe提出了代码运行工具的安全性问题，引发了对使用便捷性和安全风险之间平衡的讨论。

争议焦点：
• Anthropic的API定价是否过高，以及其是否能通过降低推理成本保持竞争力。
• 使用便捷的代码运行工具是否会带来不可接受的安全风险。

ccusage
Analyze your Claude Code token usage and costs from local JSONL files — incredibly fast and informative!
Installation
Quick Start (Recommended)
Thanks to ccusage's incredibly small bundle size (
), you can run it directly without installation:
#
Using bunx (recommended for speed)
bunx ccusage
#
Using npx
npx ccusage@latest
#
Using deno (with security flags)
deno run -E -R=
$HOME
/.claude/projects/ -S=homedir -N=
'
raw.githubusercontent.com:443
'
npm:ccusage@latest
💡
Tip
: We recommend using
bunx
instead of
npx
for a massive speed improvement!
Local Installation (Optional)
Since ccusage has such a small bundle size, installation is entirely optional:
npm install -g ccusage
Usage
#
Basic usage
ccusage
#
Show daily report (default)
ccusage daily
#
Daily token usage and costs
ccusage monthly
#
Monthly aggregated report
ccusage session
#
Usage by conversation session
ccusage blocks
#
5-hour billing windows
#
Live monitoring
ccusage blocks --live
#
Real-time usage dashboard
#
Filters and options
ccusage daily --since 20250525 --until 20250530
ccusage daily --json
#
JSON output
ccusage daily --breakdown
#
Per-model cost breakdown
Features
📊
Daily Report
: View token usage and costs aggregated by date
📅
Monthly Report
: View token usage and costs aggregated by month
💬
Session Report
: View usage grouped by conversation sessions
⏰
5-Hour Blocks Report
: Track usage within Claude's billing windows with active block monitoring
📈
Live Monitoring
: Real-time dashboard showing active session progress, token burn rate, and cost projections with
blocks --live
🤖
Model Tracking
: See which Claude models you're using (Opus, Sonnet, etc.)
📊
Model Breakdown
: View per-model cost breakdown with
--breakdown
flag
📅
Date Filtering
: Filter reports by date range using
--since
and
--until
📁
Custom Path
: Support for custom Claude data directory locations
🎨
Beautiful Output
: Colorful table-formatted display with automatic responsive layout
📱
Smart Tables
: Automatic compact mode for narrow terminals (< 100 characters) with essential columns
📋
Enhanced Model Display
: Model names shown as bulleted lists for better readability
📄
JSON Output
: Export data in structured JSON format with
--json
💰
Cost Tracking
: Shows costs in USD for each day/month/session
🔄
Cache Token Support
: Tracks and displays cache creation and cache read tokens separately
🌐
Offline Mode
: Use pre-cached pricing data without network connectivity with
--offline
(Claude models only)
🔌
MCP Integration
: Built-in Model Context Protocol server for integration with other tools
🚀
Ultra-Small Bundle
: Unlike other CLI tools, we pay extreme attention to bundle size - incredibly small even without minification!

data.title: Debcraft – Easiest way to modify and build Debian packages
data.author: pabs3
data.article_summary:
Debian 打包因其复杂性和繁琐的维护任务，常让新贡献者望而却步。Debcraft 是一个自动化工具，旨在简化打包过程，帮助新手和老手更好地跟踪源代码和构建产物的变更。与 RPM 或 APK 不同，Debian 打包使用多个声明式文件，而非单一的程序化脚本，这提高了系统的稳健性，但要求用户理解各文件的语法和各工具的交互。常见抱怨包括工具繁多、文档过时且不一致、缺乏最佳实践等。

Debcraft 通过使用 Git、git-buildpackage 和 Linux 容器（如 Docker 和 Podman），使开发者无需在 Debian 系统上开发。它简化了构建、测试和更新包的过程，提供 `debcraft build`、`debcraft shell` 和 `debcraft test` 等命令，便于调试和自动化改进包质量（如使用 lintian 自动修复问题）。最终，`debcraft release` 命令帮助将包上传至 PPA 或官方 Debian 存档。

44611223.article_content:
Debian packaging is notoriously hard. Far too many new contributors give up while trying, and many long-time contributors leave due to burnout from having to do too many thankless maintenance tasks. Some just skip testing their changes properly because it feels like too much toil.
Debcraft
is my attempt to solve this by automating all the boring stuff, and making it easier to learn the correct practices and helping new and old packagers better track changes in both source code and build artifacts.
The challenge of declarative packaging code
Unlike how
rpm
or
apk
packages are done, the
deb package
sources by design avoid having one massive procedural packaging recipe. Instead, the packaging is defined in multiple declarative files in the
debian/
subdirectory. For example, instead of a script running
install -m 755 bin/btop /usr/bin/btop
there is a file
debian/btop.install
containing the line
usr/bin/btop
.
This makes the overall system more robust and reliable, and allows, for example, extensive static analysis to find problems without having to build the package. The notable exception is the
debian/rules
file, which contains procedural code that can modify any aspect of the package build. Almost all other files are declarative.
Benefits include, among others, that the effect of a Debian-wide policy change can be relatively easily predicted by scanning what attributes and configurations all packages have declared.
The drawback is that to understand the syntax and meaning of each file, one must understand which build tools read which files and traverse potentially multiple layers of abstraction. In my view, this is the root cause for most of the perceived complexity.
Common complaints about .deb packaging
Related to the above, people learning Debian packaging frequently voice the following complaints:
Debian has too many tools to learn, often with overlapping or duplicate functionality.
Too much outdated and inconsistent documentation that makes learning the numerous tools needlessly hard.
Lack of documentation of the generally agreed best practices, mainly due to Debian’s reluctance as a project to pick one tool and deprecate the alternatives.
Multiple layers of abstraction and lack of clarity on what any single change in the
debian/
subdirectory leads to in the final package.
Requirement of Debian packages to be developed on a Debian system.
How Debcraft solves (some of) this
Debcraft
is intentionally opinionated for the sake of simplicity, and makes heavy use of git, git-buildpackage, and most importantly Linux containers, supporting both Docker and Podman.
By using containers, Debcraft frees the user from the requirement of having to run Debian. This makes .deb packaging more accessible to developers running some other Linux distro or even Mac or Windows (with WSL). Of course we want developers to run Debian (or a derivative like Ubuntu) but we want them even more to build, test and ship their software as .deb. Even for Debian/Ubuntu users having everything done inside clean hermetic containers of the latest target distribution version will yield more robust, secure and reproducible builds and tests. All containers are built automatically on-the-fly using best practices for layer caching, making everything easy and fast.
Debcraft has simple commands to make it easy to build, rebuild, test and update packages.
The most fundamental command is
debcraft build
, which will not only build the package but also fetch the sources if not already present, and with flags such as
--distribution
or
--source-only
build for any requested Debian or Ubuntu release, or generate source packages only for Debian or PPA upload purposes.
For ease of use, the output is colored and includes helpful explanations on what is being done, and suggests relevant Debian documentation for more information.
Most importantly, the build artifacts, along with various logs, are stored in separate directories, making it easy to compare before and after to see what changed as a result of the code or dependency updates (utilizing
diffoscope
among others).
While the above helps to debug successful builds, there is also the
debcraft shell
command to make debugging failed builds significantly easier by dropping into a shell where one can run various
dh
commands one-by-one.
Once the build works, testing autopkgtests is as easy as running
debcraft test
. As with all other commands, Debcraft is smart enough to read information like the target distribution from the
debian/changelog
entry.
When the package is ready to be released, there is the
debcraft release
command that will create the Debian source package in the correct format and facilitate uploading it either to your Personal Package Archive (PPA) or if you are a Debian Developer to the official Debian archive.
Automatically improve and update packages
Additionally, the command
debcraft improve
will try to fix all issues that are possible to address automatically. It utilizes, among others,
lintian

data.title: C++: Zero-cost static initialization
data.author: oecumena
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了C和C++中函数内静态变量的使用及其初始化机制。静态变量具有静态存储期，其初始化在C中是编译时常量，而在C++中则有更复杂的初始化分类，包括静态初始化和动态初始化等。对于块作用域的静态变量，C++标准规定其初始化在首次执行到声明时进行，且如果初始化过程中抛出异常，则下次进入声明时会重试。

文章还详细介绍了编译器如何通过内部标志和同步对象来确保静态变量的线程安全初始化，并展示了相关的汇编代码示例。尽管初始化后访问静态变量仍涉及一定的开销，但通过利用UNIX链接器的一个特性，可以完全消除这种额外成本，使块级静态变量与文件级静态变量一样高效。这涉及将静态对象放置在一个专用链接段中，利用链接器自动提供的符号来管理初始化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：C++中静态变量的初始化与优化

不同观点：
• **关于静态变量初始化的时机**：
  - [ot] 认为仅在极热路径（extraordinarily hot paths）上进行此类优化才有意义，并提到在ARM上原子加载需要内存屏障，开销较大，而在x86上无区别。
  - [kazinator] 提出块作用域静态变量应尽可能在程序启动时初始化，而不是等到函数被调用时，以减少麻烦的情况。

• **关于编译器对代码布局的处理**：
  - [ot] 指出GCC和Clang在代码布局上表现不佳，特别是在内联慢路径问题上，建议通过跳转到冷代码段来优化。
  - [pbsd] 反驳了对静态变量访问开销的担忧，指出只有在变量初始化时才有并发保护，初始化完成后不再有额外开销。

• **关于非可移植代码与全局变量的使用**：
  - [foota] 提到使用链接器特性实现静态计数器数组，但发现Mac OS不兼容，需特殊处理。
  - [forrestthewoods] 强烈反对使用非可移植代码，建议避免使用可变全局变量，编写符合标准且可移植的C/C++代码。

补充讨论：
• **静态变量初始化的潜在行为变化**：
  - [Someone] 提到如果函数从未被调用，包含的静态变量可能永远不会被初始化，从而改变程序行为。

• **GCC扩展与C++特性**：
  - [naruhodo] 介绍GCC的Statement Expressions扩展，并指出C++11后可通过lambda实现类似效果。

44570113.article_content:
"
Усердие все превозмогает!
"
К. Прутков,
Мысли и афоризмы, I
, 84
In C and C++ a static variable can be defined in a function scope:
int foo() {
static int counter = 1;
printf("foo() has been called %i times.\n", counter++);
...
}
Technically, this defines
counter
as an object of
static storage duration
that is allocated not within the function activation frame (which is typically on the stack, but can be on the heap for a
coroutine
), but as a global object. This is often used to shift computational cost out of the hot path, by precomputing some state and storing it in a static object.
When exactly a static object is initialised?
For C this question is vacuous, because the initialiser must be a
compile-time constant
, so the actual value of the static object is embedded in the compiled binary and is always valid.
C++ has a bizarrely complicated taxonomy of
initialisations
. There is
static
initialisation, which roughly corresponds to C initialisation, subdivided into constant-initialisation and zero-initialisation. Then there is
dynamic
initialisation, further divided into unordered, partially-ordered and ordered categories. None of these, however, captures our case: for block-local variables, the Standard has a special sub-section in "Declaration statement" [
stmt.dcl.4
]:
Dynamic initialization of a block-scope variable with static storage duration  or thread storage duration is performed the first time control passes through  its declaration; such a variable is considered initialized upon the completion  of its initialization. If the initialization exits by throwing an exception,  the initialization is not complete, so it will be tried again the next time  control enters the declaration. If control enters the declaration concurrently  while the variable is being initialized, the concurrent execution shall wait  for completion of the initialization. If control re-enters the declaration  recursively while the variable is being initialized, the behavior is  undefined.
For example in
struct Bar {
Bar() : var(1) {}
int var;
};
int foo(int x) {
static Bar b{};
return b.var + 1;
}
the constructor for
b
should be called exactly once when
foo()
is called the first time. This initialisation semantics is very close (sans the exceptions part) to
pthread_once
()
. It is clear that the compiler must add some sort of an internal flag to check whether the initialisation has already been performed and some synchronisation object to serialise concurrent calls to
foo()
[
godbolt
]:
foo(int):
push    rbp
mov     rbp, rsp
sub     rsp, 16
mov     DWORD PTR [rbp-4], edi
movzx   eax, BYTE PTR guard variable for foo(int)::b[rip]
test    al, al
sete    al
test    al, al
je      .L3
mov     edi, OFFSET FLAT:guard variable for foo(int)::b
call    __cxa_guard_acquire
test    eax, eax
setne   al
test    al, al
je      .L3
mov     edi, OFFSET FLAT:foo(int)::b
call    Bar::Bar() [complete object constructor]
mov     edi, OFFSET FLAT:guard variable for foo(int)::b
call    __cxa_guard_release
.L3:
mov     eax, DWORD PTR foo(int)::b[rip]
add     eax, 1
leave
ret
This corresponds roughly to the following code:
int foo(int x) {
static Bar b{};
static std::atomic<int> __b_guard = 0;
if (__cxa_guard_acquire(&__b_guard) != 0) {
new (&b) Bar{}; /* Construct b in-place. */
__cxa_guard_release(&__b_guard)
}
return b.var + 1;
}
Here
__b_guard
(
guard variable for foo(int)::b
in assembly) is the flag variable added by the compiler.
__cxa_guard_acquire
()
is a suprisingly complex function, which includes its own synchronisation mechanism implemented directly on top of the raw Linux
futex syscall
.
Even after the static variable has been initialised, the overhead of accessing it is still considerable: a function call to
__cxa_guard_acquire()
, plus
atomic_load_explicit(&__b_guard, memory_order::acquire)
in
__cxa_guard_acquire()
. On ARM, such atomic load incurs a memory barrier---a fairly expensive operation.
Can this additional cost be reduced? Yes, in fact it can be completely eliminated, making block-level static variables exactly as efficient as file-level ones. For this we need a certain old, but little-known feature of UNIX linkers. From GNU binutils
documentation
(beware than in the old versions the terminating symbol is mistakenly referred to as
__end_SECNAME
):
If an output section’s name is the same as the input section’s name and is representable as a C identifier, then the linker will automatically
PROVIDE
two symbols:
__start_SECNAME
and
__stop_SECNAME
, where
SECNAME
is the name of the section. These indicate the start address and end address of the output section respectively. Note: most section names are not representable as C identifiers because they contain a ‘.’ character.
(Solaris linker calls them "Encapsulation Symbols", see
here
.)
The idea is the following: instead of defining a block-level static instance of
Bar
, define a trivially-initialisable object of a size sufficient to hold an instance of
Bar
in a dedicated section
44570113.article_summary:
文章讨论了C和C++中函数内静态变量的使用及其初始化机制。静态变量具有静态存储期，其初始化在C中是编译时常量，而在C++中则有更复杂的初始化分类，包括静态初始化和动态初始化等。对于块作用域的静态变量，C++标准规定其初始化在首次执行到声明时进行，且如果初始化过程中抛出异常，则下次进入声明时会重试。

文章还详细介绍了编译器如何通过内部标志和同步对象来确保静态变量的线程安全初始化，并展示了相关的汇编代码示例。尽管初始化后访问静态变量仍涉及一定的开销，但通过利用UNIX链接器的一个特性，可以完全消除这种额外成本，使块级静态变量与文件级静态变量一样高效。这涉及将静态对象放置在一个专用链接段中，利用链接器自动提供的符号来管理初始化。

主要讨论点：美国政府机构和监管体系的现状及其问题

不同观点：
• jleyank认为美国的三权分立体系原本应通过各分支间的 tension 维持平衡，但现在体系似乎基于信念运行，一旦有人试图破坏，便迅速瓦解。这表明对体系的原有设计过于天真。
• consumer451指出，像FAA和EPA这样的监管机构的法规往往是基于血的教训制定的，尤其是环境法规。他认为人们不应轻视这些法规的价值，并质疑是否有人真的认为尼克松成立EPA是为了打击大企业。
• guru4consulting对EPA的看法与公众不同，认为EPA并不是如公众所想的臃肿低效，而是有许多优秀员工。他指出真正的问题是大公司通过联邦采购程序交付劣质结果并规避法律。
• globalview提出了一种从不同角度看待问题的观点，认为部分选民可能不再相信EPA等机构是中立的科学仲裁者，而是将其视为推动政治议程的工具。因此，某些人可能将机构的解散视为“拆除有偏见的系统”而非“破坏”。

• Herring将当前局势与历史上的阶级和种族问题联系起来，认为通过挑拨社会群体间的对立，政客得以推行有利于富人的政策。

• bamboozled和oulipo用情绪化的语言表达了对现状的强烈不满。
• wpm简单表达了对当前局势的失望。
• dffee对评论中的一致意见表示怀疑，提出需要反思原有体系是否真的完美，并提出对更好体系的探索。

data.title: Intel Announces It's Shutting Down Clear Linux
data.author: gpi
data.article_summary: 英特尔宣布将关闭其性能优化的Clear Linux操作系统。Clear Linux在过去十年中展示了在x86_64硬件上开箱即用的卓越性能，不仅在英特尔平台上表现出色，在AMD平台上也同样优异。但由于英特尔的成本削减措施，Clear Linux即将被终止。英特尔已发布声明，将立即停止对Clear Linux的安全补丁、更新和维护，GitHub库也将被归档为只读模式。英特尔建议用户尽快迁移到其他活跃的Linux发行版。尽管如此，英特尔表示仍将深度参与Linux生态系统，继续支持和贡献开源项目。Clear Linux的关闭也伴随着几位关键工程师的离职和其他重组措施，引发了对英特尔开源和Linux项目的未来担忧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对企业和开源项目的贡献以及Clear Linux和Intel相关技术的评价

不同观点：
• burnt-resistor认为，企业通常是寄生性的，对自由和开源软件（FLOSS）项目的支持不足。他们关注的是新功能的增加，而不是可用性、简洁性或完善性。
• codpiece回顾了Clear Linux曾经的优点，指出其团队过去的高度响应性，但也提到社区氛围的变化，并提到其他发行版采用了他们的内核优化。
• johnklos对Intel的技术提出批评，认为Intel需要关注CPU的修复，并提到Amiga仍在发展，而Clear Linux、32位x86和macOS on x86正在消亡。
• melling认为Intel已经落后，错过了AI boom，并希望Intel能扭转局面。
• ksec同意Intel需要专注，并认为Intel仍然显得非常臃肿。
• vondur对Clear Linux的优化表示赞赏，希望有人能继续其内核优化工作。
• CoastalCoder表示只要Intel继续维护VTune，他就满意，因为这是他选择Intel芯片的重要原因。
• fsckboy建议AMD应该接手并继续推进Clear Linux项目。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及Clear Linux的兴衰及其社区的变化，部分用户对其技术贡献表示认可，并对未来发展表示关注。
• 对Intel的批评主要集中在CPU性能、功耗和安全性问题上，部分用户对其未来发展持悲观或期望态度。
• 争议的焦点包括企业对开源项目的贡献是否足够，以及Intel在技术发展上的战略和执行能力。
• 有建议提出让其他公司或社区接手相关技术项目，显示出对现有技术生态的期望和潜在的替代方案。

44611270.article_content:
Intel Announces It's Shutting Down Clear Linux
Written by
Michael Larabel
in
Intel
on 18 July 2025 at 06:01 PM EDT.
31 Comments
The most depressing news of the week: Intel is ending their performance-optimized Clear Linux distribution. Over the past decade the
Clear Linux
operating system has shown what's possible with out-of-the-box performance on x86_64 hardware... Not just for Intel platforms but even showing extremely great performance results on AMD x86_64 too. But with the cost-cutting going on at Intel, Clear Linux is now being sunset.
Intel put out
a statement
that Clear Linux is being shutdown:
"After years of innovation and community collaboration, we’re ending support for Clear Linux OS. Effective immediately, Intel will no longer provide security patches, updates, or maintenance for Clear Linux OS, and the Clear Linux OS GitHub repository will be archived in read-only mode. So, if you’re currently using Clear Linux OS, we strongly recommend planning your migration to another actively maintained Linux distribution as soon as possible to ensure ongoing security and stability.
Rest assured that Intel remains deeply invested in the Linux ecosystem, actively supporting and contributing to various open-source projects and Linux distributions to enable and optimize for Intel hardware.
A heartfelt thank you to every developer, user, and contributor who helped shape Clear Linux OS over the last 10 years. Your feedback and contributions have been invaluable."
Heartbreaking. In recent years I heard a few times of Clear Linux potentially being on the chopping-block due to cost-cutting at Intel and trying to emphasize out-of-the-box performance for the major Linux distributions and getting more of their work upstreamed as well. Today though it's finally been made official.
Clear Linux has delivered many great out-of-the-box performance optimizations for Linux systems and shown what can be done for packaging with profile guided optimizations / link-time optimizations, various kernel tweaks, and other innovations over the years. At least the likes of CachyOS have picked up some of these optimizations. Intel engineers are also working with other major Linux distributions on enhancing their Linux distribution performance too. But those details and whether they will be ramping up those efforts or not remain unclear.
This caps off a week where
a very prominent Linux engineer left Intel
,
an upstream Linux driver is now orphaned over another engineer departure
, and various other Intel software engineers working on open-source/Linux also let go as part of the latest restructuring at Intel.

data.title: Bun adds pnpm-style isolated installation mode
data.author: nateb2022
data.article_summary:
这篇文章主要介绍了在Bun的包管理工具中实现"nodeLinker": "isolated"选项的更新。该选项提供类似pnpm的隔离安装模式，防止幽灵依赖并支持并行安装包。主要变更包括：

1. 支持在package.json中配置`workspaces.nodeLinker: "isolated"`。
2. 包被安装在`node_modules/.bun/`目录下的隔离结构中。
3. 通过符号链接将`node_modules/<package>`链接到实际包位置。
4. 处理范围包、同伴依赖和工作区等。

代码通过了一系列测试验证，包括基本依赖安装、范围包、传递依赖、循环依赖、文件夹依赖、工作区支持和符号链接结构验证。此外，文章还提到了一些测试失败的情况和如何在本地尝试此PR。最终，这些更改被合并到了main分支。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Bun v1.2.19 发布、Bun的性能和功能、在monorepo中使用Bun的可行性、Bun的底层技术原理

不同观点：
• **Jarred** 提到Bun v1.2.19版本即将发布，但因为Windows上的一个bug，发布被推迟。他解释了isolated install模式的性能优势，尤其是在Windows上（安装速度提升10倍或20倍），并提供了提前试用该功能的方法。他还指出isolated installs在monorepos中的可靠性提升。

• **dsabanin** 对Bun的shell脚本API表示赞赏，认为其在TypeScript中使用起来非常方便和符合人体工学，比bash更直观，且支持单文件和管道等功能，大幅提升了编写实用脚本的体验。

• **papichulo2023** 分享了自己将bash脚本迁移到Bun的JavaScript环境的积极体验，强调了Bun的简单性、速度和无需外部依赖的数据库脚本功能，并表示不再需要频繁重学bash语法。

• **tekkk** 关注在pnpm monorepo中使用Bun的可行性，表示虽然对Bun感兴趣，但担心迁移后可能会遇到功能缺失，特别是与monorepo中运行特定脚本相关的问题。

• **markl42** 希望了解Bun在底层技术上与现状的不同之处，寻求更深入的技术解释。

• **Alifatisk** 对Bun的发展表示赞赏，认为Bun正逐渐成为JavaScript生态系统中的全能解决方案，并对开发者Jarred的技术能力表示钦佩。

补充讨论：
• 关于Bun在不同操作系统上的性能差异存在讨论，Jarred提到Windows上的性能提升显著，而macOS和Linux上的影响较小或无影响。
• 用户对Bun在monorepo中的应用存在疑虑，特别是其与pnpm等工具的兼容性和功能完整性。
• 一些用户对Bun的易用性和功能丰富性表示高度认可，尤其是在替代bash脚本和简化开发流程方面。

争议焦点：
• 目前的主要争议在于Bun在monorepo中的可靠性和功能完整性，特别是对于复杂项目（如pnpm monorepo）的支持程度。用户担心迁移后可能遇到功能缺失或兼容性问题。

What does this PR do?
This PR implements the
"nodeLinker": "isolated"
option for
bun install
, providing a pnpm-style isolated installation mode that prevents phantom dependencies and and enables installing packages in parallel.
Key features:
Adds support for
workspaces.nodeLinker: "isolated"
configuration in package.json
Installs packages in an isolated structure under
node_modules/.bun/
directory
Creates symlinks from
node_modules/<package>
to the actual packages in
.bun/<package>@<version>/node_modules/<package>
Properly handles scoped packages, peer dependencies, and workspaces
Directory structure example:
node_modules/
├── my-dependency -> .bun/my-dependency@1.0.0/node_modules/my-dependency
└── .bun/
├── my-dependency@1.0.0/
│   └── node_modules/
│       ├── my-dependency/
│       └── sub-dep -> ../../sub-dep@2.0.0/node_modules/sub-dep
└── sub-dep@2.0.0/
└── node_modules/
└── sub-dep/
Configuration:
{
"workspaces"
: {
"nodeLinker"
:
"
isolated
"
//
or "hoisted" for the previous behavior
}
}

data.author: neehao
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了广告在经济学中的两个积极作用——提供信息和传递质量信号——以及互联网如何改变这些作用。互联网极大降低了搜索成本，但也削弱了广告作为质量信号的功能。文章列举了五大摩擦因素，使得低质量卖家能通过付费广告与高质量商品竞争：可随意丢弃的品牌身份、按成果付费（CPA）的定价模式、宽松的退货政策、评分压缩和消费者依赖价格判断质量。这些因素共同导致市场陷入“欺诈者均衡”，即低质量商品通过广告与高质量商品共存。文章提出了一些解决方案，如持久的制造商ID、根据退货调整的CPA附加费、广告保证金和重新启动检测等，以恢复信号功能。尽管存在这些问题，市场并未崩溃，原因包括宽松的退货政策、低生产成本、多样化需求和平台收入与广告 congestion 相关。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电商平台上的产品评价、广告设计、消费者决策以及平台与制造商之间的利益冲突。

不同观点：
• Cornholio认为，将产品评价与制造商而非商店绑定的建议难以实施。制造商与亚马逊之间存在根本利益冲突，因为制造商希望完全控制销售渠道并自行设置促销和折扣，而亚马逊则希望品牌分销商相互竞争以提供最低价格。这种冲突导致制造商不愿意为次级渠道销售的产品背书，也不会合作进行"全球评分"机制。

• Somat指出星级评分系统的问题，认为评分集中在4.3到4.9之间，使得消费者难以区分产品优劣。他建议将0设为中间值，通过正负评分来表达对产品是否符合预期。

• Zkmon对当前电视广告的设计表示不满，认为这些广告为了吸引注意力而变得怪异和有害，常常让观众难以理解产品本身。他担心这种广告趋势反映了广告设计者对注意力的过度追求。

• CommenterPerson作为消费者，表示面对复杂的购买环境，选择延迟购买或不购买，除非急需。这种策略避免了在混乱的电商环境中做出决策。

• Mattlondon质疑1985年的研究关于价格作为质量指标的有效性，认为如今大多数产品都是大规模生产，质量差异不大。消费者倾向于依赖视频平台如YouTube来判断产品质量，但仍需警惕付费评论。

• Esperent认为Oatly的广告是一种"humblebrag"策略，通过不直接说明产品优点来强化品牌形象，吸引那些已经考虑转换到非乳制品的人群。

• Soared对某些广告公式表示困惑，认为这些公式看似认真却更像喜剧。

• Mrkramer指出IKEA家具评价多为高分，怀疑低分评价被删除或不满消费者不愿评价。

• ArtTimeInvestor反驳CPA定价能消除竞争压力的观点，认为广告空间竞争依然激烈，出价最高者得。

• Jrm4认为广告中情感诉求比信息或逻辑更重要。

• Mrala简单说明CPA代表按行动付费。

• Sgt101提问消费者如何获取有用信息以做出更好的购买决策，建议使用其他信息渠道或信任次级销售网站。

• Maartenscholl将讨论与"市场柠檬车"故事联系起来，认为需要研究买家对品牌质量的信念。

• Dreamcompiler引用Doctorow的"enshittification"理论，描述无品牌供应商如何在亚马逊等平台垄断下获利。

• Seydor认为像Temu这样的平台成功是因为搜索结果简单直接，产品价格低廉，减少了选择困难和广告干扰。

补充讨论：
• 电商平台上评分系统的有效性和改进建议。
• 广告设计对消费者注意力的影响及潜在反感。
• 消费者在复杂电商环境中的决策策略。
• 制造商与平台之间的利益冲突及对产品评价的影响。
• 不同广告策略的效果及情感诉求的重要性。

44612023.article_content:
Economists credit ads with two welfare‑enhancing roles:
Informative
– trimming search costs (
Stigler 1961
(pdf)).
Signaling
– In classic models, high-quality sellers are more willing to incur large, sunk ad costs because they expect to recoup them through future sales—especially in experience-good markets where quality is learned over time (
Nelson 1974
).
Milgrom and Roberts (1986)
formalize this idea: when ad spend is costly and more valuable to better firms, it can serve as a credible signal of quality.
Internet upended the first role—search is instant—but also weakened the second.
Five Frictions That Flatten the Signal
Disposable brand identities
Launching a fresh storefront requires packaging, photography, and a seed set of paid or incentivized reviews; yet, those outlays are tiny relative to the lifetime margin on a successful listing. Because tarnished names can be retired cheaply, long‑run reputation no longer disciplines bad actors.
CPA pricing removes the burn
Most major ad systems now let advertisers pay only when a sale or lead occurs (Target CPA in Google Ads, Cost‑per‑Result goals in Meta’s Advantage+ campaigns, goal‑based bidding in Amazon DSP). With spending converted from
sunk
to
variable
, even low‑quality sellers can fund promotion from day‑one revenue.
Light‑touch returns & the “Frequently Returned” tag
Seamless returns cap consumer harm, but seller penalties are modest: a restocking fee, a metrics ding, or Amazon’s “Frequently Returned Item” badge—issued only after damage is done. Only the worst lemons are fully delisted, leaving plenty of mediocre goods in play.
Ratings compression
Star ratings on major platforms increasingly cluster between 4.3 and 4.9, leaving buyers little room to distinguish products. Part of this stems from review manipulation—Amazon
blocked >250 million suspected fake reviews
in 2023 alone, indicating the size of the problem.
Heuristic‑driven shoppers
Deprived of credible signals, buyers default to the price–quality heuristic—higher price means better goods (Monroe  &  Krishnan 1985). Sellers respond by listing identical inventory at staggered prices across multiple storefronts.
These frictions reinforce one another: CPA funding keeps every storefront bidding; fake reviews mask quality gaps; disposable brands dodge reputational blowback; and behavioural heuristics close the sale—locking the marketplace into what we call the grifter equilibrium.
A Sock Search in Action
Search
“ankle socks”
on Amazon:
Sponsored slots dominate; brands are unfamiliar.
Ratings hover around 4.5; product photos are interchangeable.
Prices span a wide range without visible changes in features.
Formalising the Grifter Equilibrium
A. Setup
Symbol
Meaning
(p)
Posted price (assumed equal across types for clarity)
(m_H, m_L)
Unit cost for high‑ and low‑quality goods ((m_H > m_L))
(\tau)
CPA take‑rate (identical across sellers unless platform surcharges)
(\phi)
Probability a low‑quality sale triggers a penalty/return
(R)
Expected penalty per flagged lemon
(k)
Cost of opening a new storefront (small but positive)
B. Per‑sale profits
$$[
\pi_H = p(1-\tau) - m_H, \qquad
\pi_L = p(1-\tau) - m_L - \phi R .
]$$
C. Advertising condition for low‑quality sellers
$$[
\pi_L > 0
;\Longleftrightarrow;
m_L + \phi R < p(1-\tau).
]$$
Ultra‑cheap production and modest penalties make this inequality easy to satisfy, so lemons advertise alongside premium goods.
D. Dynamic relaunch option
If poor feedback eventually sinks a storefront, the seller pays (R), incurs a small relaunch cost (k), and restarts the cycle. Unless (k) or (R) become large, the net present value of “being a lemon” remains positive, sustaining a pooling equilibrium in which ad spend reveals little.
Escape Hatches
Restoring signalling requires a cost that lemons cannot shirk:
Persistent manufacturer IDs
– reputation follows the factory, not the storefront.
Return‑adjusted CPA surcharges
– raise ($\tau$) when ($\phi R$) climbs.
Escrowed ad bonds
– forfeited if defect or return metrics exceed benchmarks.
Relaunch detection
– inventory‑fingerprint matching to raise ($k$).
Why the Marketplace Doesn't Implode
Return valve caps—but doesn’t erase—consumer pain.
Generous return policies and Amazon’s “Frequently Returned Item” badge let buyers jettison the worst lemons. Hassle costs remain, but catastrophic disutility is rare.
Ultra‑low unit costs keep lemons profitable.
When socks cost $2 to make and the CPA take‑rate is 20 %, sellers can survive double‑digit return rates and still clear margin.
Heterogeneous, often low‑stakes demand.
For gym gear, kids’ camp supplies, or one‑off gadgets, shoppers accept higher quality uncertainty in exchange for speed and price, muting the penalty for mediocre goods.
Platform revenue is tied to congestion—up to a point.
Amazon collects a fee on every ad click
and
every sale, so a crowded, ad‑dense marketplace boosts short‑run revenue. The company does police egregious abuse to protect long‑run customer trust, but the

data.title: Show HN: OrioleDB Beta12 Features and Benchmarks
data.author: akorotkov
data.article_summary: OrioleDB是PostgreSQL的存储扩展，旨在解决其可扩展性瓶颈，提升多核CPU和高性能存储系统的利用率。近期更新包括：支持非B-tree索引类型、回滚数据库近期更改、支持表空间和fillfactor、新增空间利用统计函数`orioledb_tree_stat()`，以及支持超过32列的表。性能改进包括更高效的存储分配、行级和页级撤销日志的分离、主键查找的定制扫描节点，以及B-tree内页导航的优化。通过TPC-C风格的基准测试（使用go-tpc和sysbench工具）显示，OrioleDB在多种实例类型下的性能显著优于PostgreSQL默认的Heap存储引擎，特别是在高吞吐量在线事务处理（OLTP）场景中。例如，在16xl实例下，OrioleDB的tpmC达到218,716，而Heap仅为83,653。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Postgres数据库是否会采纳新的存储引擎（OrioleDB）以及其潜在影响和实现方式

不同观点：
• [atombender] 认为OrioleDB的性能提升非常显著，尤其是其基于undo log的系统设计可以避免Postgres当前MVCC机制导致的bloat问题。虽然这种设计可能在读取未提交数据时牺牲一些读性能，但整体上认为这种设计更优。然而，他质疑Postgres核心团队是否会因为保守而不接受如此大的改动，尤其是替换现有的MVCC机制。

• [akorotkov] 提到了OrioleDB新版本中的fastpath树搜索功能，可以加速密集键值查找的工作负载，并预告了即将发布的博客文章。

• [ksec] 表达了对OrioleDB成为Postgres官方部分的期望，认为这将使开源SQL数据库系统更加强大且无需过多定制，尤其是在结合Planetscale的工作时。

• [rickette] 关心Postgres的全文搜索（FTS）功能是否会从OrioleDB存储引擎中受益。

• [ololobus] 询问OrioleDB是否需要核心补丁，还是可以在标准上游Postgres中作为扩展安装。

• [kabes] 询问OrioleDB作为Postgres扩展的稳定性以及距离正式发布还有多远。

• [znpy] 关心OrioleDB如何融入当前的数据库生态系统，特别是能否与其他扩展（如Amazon最近发布的pgactive）一起使用。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Postgres核心团队是否会接受OrioleDB作为主要存储引擎，尤其是考虑到团队在引入大改动时的保守态度。
• 评论中还涉及OrioleDB的具体技术实现细节，如fastpath树搜索的性能提升，以及其在不同工作负载下的适用性。
• 用户对OrioleDB的安装方式和与其他扩展的兼容性也表示了关注。

44570389.article_content:
Since our
last public update
, OrioleDB has continued to evolve with a series of new releases. These updates refine the core engine, extend functionality, and improve performance across a range of workloads. Together, they move us closer to a beta release and lay the groundwork for broader adoption.
What is OrioleDB?
​
OrioleDB is a PostgreSQL storage extension that implements a custom
Table Access Method
as a drop‑in replacement for the default Heap storage engine. It is designed to address scalability bottlenecks in PostgreSQL’s buffer manager and reduces the WAL, enabling better utilization of modern multi-core CPUs and high‑performance storage systems.
By rethinking core components such as MVCC, page caching, and checkpoints, OrioleDB improves throughput and predictability in transactional workloads without altering PostgreSQL’s user-facing behavior.
What’s New in OrioleDB?
​
Building on this foundation, recent releases have introduced several user-facing enhancements:
Support for non‑
B-tree
index types
on OrioleDB tables.
Support for
rewinding recent changes
in the database.
Support for tablespaces.
fillfactor
support for OrioleDB tables and indexes.
orioledb_tree_stat()
SQL function for space utilization statistics.
Support for tables with more than 32 columns.
These additions improve OrioleDB/PostgreSQL compatibility and provide more flexibility for workloads with diverse schema and indexing requirements.
Performance improvements
​
Alongside these user‑facing additions, significant performance improvements have been made:
Storage and Transactional Efficiency
​
Sparse file support for more efficient storage allocation.
Separation of row‑level and page‑level undo logs.
Optimizations to avoid undo records for insertions into tables created by the same transaction
Query and Index Performance
​
Custom scan node for primary key lookups, reducing redundant index searches.
Faster
B-tree
inner page navigation for improved index performance.
To assess the impact of these changes, we benchmarked OrioleDB against PostgreSQL’s default Heap storage engine using
TPC-C
style workloads with
go-tpc
and
sysbench
. These tests measure CPU and IO scalability under mixed read‑write conditions and evaluate how OrioleDB’s architecture performs in transactional workloads.
Benchmarks
​
TPC-C is a standard benchmark for measuring how well databases handle high-throughput online transaction processing (OLTP). The test uses a database with 10 tables and includes five types of transactions:
NewOrder – for creating new orders
Payment – for processing payments
OrderStatus – for checking order status
Delivery – for handling deliveries
StockLevel – for analyzing inventory
Benchmark Infrastructure
​
We’ve run all of these instances on a
Supabase 2XL Instance using io2 storage
unless otherwise specified. Postgres configuration options use Supabase’s defaults.
The instance used for running the load test was located in the same AWS region (but in an different AZ) as the Supabase database to reduce the side effects of network latency, and to keep the scenario realistic.
We ran three different tools to assess Oriole beta12: go-tpc, sysbench, and OLTP.
Benchmark 1: go-tpc
​
go-tpc
is a Go-based TPC-C benchmark by PingCAP. It prioritizes performance and ease of deployment. The goal of go-tpc is a lightweight, scalable benchmarking tool for modern distributed databases.
Run the test yourself
Setup:
10,000 warehouses
1TB of data
1,000,000,000 rows in stock table
300,000,000 rows in customer, order, history tables
Instructions:
Prepare the database
./gotpc tpcc --warehouses 10000 prepare -T 100 -d postgres -U postgres -p 'password' -D postgres -H db.ref.supabase.com -P 5432 --conn-params sslmode=disable --no-check
Run the benchmark multiple times
./gotpc tpcc --warehouses 10000 run -d postgres -U postgres -p 'password' -D postgres -H db.ref.supabase.com -P 5432 --conn-params sslmode=disable -T <20,50,100,200,400> --time <100s,300s,1800s>
aggregate the results, calculate average numbers of tpmC (transactions-per-minute-C)
Results:

Benchmark 2: sysbench
​
sysbench
is a Lua-based multi-purpose benchmark tool. Includes oltp_read_write, oltp_read_only, etc., which simulate OLTP workloads. The goal is general performance testing of transactional workloads, not strict TPC-C compliance.
