data.title: The curious case of the Unix workstation layout
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了1990年代UNIX工作站的机箱布局，特别提到了Silicon Graphics的Indigo²、HP 9000系列以及DEC Alphastation。作者注意到这些高端工作站的内部设计，尤其是主板和扩展卡的布局，与当时PC机（如LPX和ATX标准）的设计有相似之处。例如，Indigo²和HP 9000 Visualize系列都采用了后置接口和左侧插卡的设计，类似于当时的PC布局。文章还提到早期DEC Alphastation采用VME总线设计，但后来的型号也出现了类似PC的设计元素，如PS/2接口和标准PC内存。作者对这种现象感到好奇，不确定是各大公司独立借鉴了PC设计，还是为了降低成本而有意为之，但认为这种趋势可能反映了PC设计对工作站的影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：计算机硬件设计的历史演变和相似性，特别是工作站和个人电脑的机箱设计、总线技术以及生产制造过程中的共性。

不同观点：
• [ChuckMcM] 认为，在计算机制造的早期，由于生产工厂有限，许多机械组件被重复使用，导致不同品牌的计算机在外观和设计上出现相似性。他还解释了NRE（非重复性工程费用）在生产工具成本摊销中的作用。
• [drewg123] 纠正了对Alphastation使用VME总线的误解，指出早期Alphastation使用的是DEC的Turbochannel技术，而非VME总线。
• [don-bright] 提到S-100总线，并提供了一些相关链接，指出这是另一种值得注意的早期计算机总线标准。
• [hapless] 提出Indigo2的设计是趋同演化的结果，由于要解决相同的设计问题（如兼容全长ISA卡的小型桌面机箱），导致不同品牌的计算机设计看起来相似。他还提到ATX标准的广泛采用使得不同架构的系统在外观上趋同。
• [grewil2] 提到Amiga 3000UX工作站，强调其运行Amiga Unix的独特性及其在GNU操作系统早期开发中的作用。
• [johnklos] 将Indigo2的设计与早期的Apple II和IBM PC进行比较，指出它们在布局上的相似性，并提到Amiga 3000的设计对后来机器的影响。
• [pinewurst] 再次纠正关于SGI Indigo和早期Alphastation使用VME总线的误解，确认它们分别使用GIO32和Turbochannel总线。
• [whartung] 讨论HP 9000 712与NeXTStation的比较，考虑其在耐用性、支持性和性能等方面的优劣。
• [sugarpimpdorsey] 指出，专有UNIX工作站的超高 proprietary 性质，使得像SGI这样的厂商能以高价出售其硬件，因为无法在普通硬件上运行IRIX。
• [toast0] 认为LPX桌面设计是一个好的设计，解释了其在扩展性和传统布局方面的优点，并提到设计的趋同现象。
• [weinzierl] 回顾了计算机从集成键盘和显示器到桌面机箱再到塔式机箱的演变过程，指出设计随着时间推移变得更小、更实用。
• [aoki] 提到90年代初PC时代的三大趋势（Pentium、PCI、多平台Windows NT），并指出许多厂商转向基于PC总线和组件的设计以提高成本竞争力。
• [amelius] 建议研究台湾计算机历史，以寻找一些设计和生产上的“缺失环节”。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是早期Alphastation是否使用VME总线，[drewg123]和[pinewurst]都明确指出其使用的是Turbochannel总线而非VME。
• 另一个讨论点是计算机设计的趋同演化现象，[hapless]和[toast0]都提到不同品牌和架构的计算机由于解决相同的设计问题而变得相似。
• [sugarpimpdorsey] 强调了专有UNIX工作站的商业模式和其高价的原因，与其他讨论中提到的硬件设计和生产成本形成对比。

44616760.article_content:
The Curious Case of the UNIX workstation layout
Posted on
2025-07-19
Contents
Background
UNIX workstations
Silicon Graphics
HP 9000
DEC Alphastation
Conclusions
Background
Cathode Ray Dude recently did an excellent video about the history of the PC case, particularly the early- and mid-1990s, and the various mainboard layouts that pre-date the ATX standard. You should watch it. Here it is.
The rest of this blog will contain some spoilers for that video.
UNIX workstations
I have a bunch of 1990's RISC/UNIX workstations. I don't really know how it happened, but I went from having literally none back in October 2024, to having:
Silicon Graphics Power IndigoÂ²
Sun Ultra 80
HP 9000 Visualize B132L+
HP 9000 Visualize C3000
HP 9000 712 (running NeXTSTEP!)
Apple PowerMac 7200/90 (ok, Mac OS 7.6 Is Not UNIX, but I could install Linux or NetBSD if I wanted to)
I also briefly had an
Alphastation 500
, but I failed to get it working so I passed it on to someone who knows much more about them than me.
And watching CRD's video. I realised something.
Silicon Graphics
The Silicon Graphics IRIS Indigo is a tower workstation of the old-school. A light make-over of the previous IRIS 4D series, it has two huge PCBs, which insert vertical into a backplane using rotating clips. I'm pretty sure it's actually a
VME bus design
, both because of that Wikipedia page but because
SGI Depot describes them
as part of the "IRIS VME Series".
(ctvoigt, CC BY-SA 3.0 DE
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/de/deed.en
, via Wikimedia Commons)
But the IndigoÂ² that came after it? Desktop case. Flat mainboard with ports on the rear. PSU on the right. Card riser on the left, with cards on the left. It takes standard PC SIMMs, and has PS/2 connectors for the keyboard and mouse. By jove it looks like LPX.
Eh, maybe it's a one-off.
HP 9000
I have wanted a PA-RISC machine for a while, but now I find myself owning three. The HP 9000 series has a long and storied history, and you should just go and read
http://openpa.net
because it is an excellent resource.
My new HP 7000 712 is the machine that HP used to port NeXTSTEP OS to PA-RISC. So, obviously, I've installed NeXTSTEP 3.3 for PA-RISC. I should probably do a whole separate piece about that, because it's retro but also alarmingly familiar to this daily macOS user.
Anyway, the Model 712 looks like this inside, and at the rear.
Definitely not LPX. Much more evocative of low-cost pizza-box Apple Machintoshes of the period, like the Macintosh LC II.
But let's look at the follow-up model, the Visualize B-Class (in this case a B132L+).
It's a single flat PCB, with connectors at the rear, a card riser on the left with cards leaning to the left. The only weird thing is that the card riser has to be high enough to clear the PSU. But look - it looks really kinda of LPX-like, right? And very different to the model that came before it.
DEC Alphastation
Early Alphastations were VME based machines. Like the Indigo, I've never had one, but I saw one at RetroFest 2025 in Swindon earlier this year.
I don't have a Creative Commons picture of the insides of a DEC 3000, but here's a website with a bunch of technical details:
https://www.chilton-computing.org.uk/ccd/mainframes/p012.htm
. It's definitely nothing like a PC.
But the Alphastation 500 I had (and failed to fix)?
Connectors at the rear. A riser, with cards on the left. Sure looks LPX inspired to me. Also those power connectors look awfully like ATX power connectors (although they don't have the ATX pinout). And we've got standard PC memory, and PS/2 connectors for the keyboard.
Conclusions
I have no conclusions here. Did Digital and HP and SGI all independently copy the Packard Bell and Dell PCs of the era? Or did they get together in some secret RISC UNIX cabal to re-use PC technolog and cut the price of entry (or, make more profit)? Or is the LPX desktop just the crab of personal computer design, and all lineages will converge here eventually. I have no idea.
But now, whenever I see a machine with ports at the back and a riser card on the left, with cards on the left, I'm going to think of CRD.
44616760.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了1990年代UNIX工作站的机箱布局，特别提到了Silicon Graphics的Indigo²、HP 9000系列以及DEC Alphastation。作者注意到这些高端工作站的内部设计，尤其是主板和扩展卡的布局，与当时PC机（如LPX和ATX标准）的设计有相似之处。例如，Indigo²和HP 9000 Visualize系列都采用了后置接口和左侧插卡的设计，类似于当时的PC布局。文章还提到早期DEC Alphastation采用VME总线设计，但后来的型号也出现了类似PC的设计元素，如PS/2接口和标准PC内存。作者对这种现象感到好奇，不确定是各大公司独立借鉴了PC设计，还是为了降低成本而有意为之，但认为这种趋势可能反映了PC设计对工作站的影响。
44616760.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：计算机硬件设计的历史演变和相似性，特别是工作站和个人电脑的机箱设计、总线技术以及生产制造过程中的共性。

不同观点：
• [ChuckMcM] 认为，在计算机制造的早期，由于生产工厂有限，许多机械组件被重复使用，导致不同品牌的计算机在外观和设计上出现相似性。他还解释了NRE（非重复性工程费用）在生产工具成本摊销中的作用。
• [drewg123] 纠正了对Alphastation使用VME总线的误解，指出早期Alphastation使用的是DEC的Turbochannel技术，而非VME总线。
• [don-bright] 提到S-100总线，并提供了一些相关链接，指出这是另一种值得注意的早期计算机总线标准。
• [hapless] 提出Indigo2的设计是趋同演化的结果，由于要解决相同的设计问题（如兼容全长ISA卡的小型桌面机箱），导致不同品牌的计算机设计看起来相似。他还提到ATX标准的广泛采用使得不同架构的系统在外观上趋同。
• [grewil2] 提到Amiga 3000UX工作站，强调其运行Amiga Unix的独特性及其在GNU操作系统早期开发中的作用。
• [johnklos] 将Indigo2的设计与早期的Apple II和IBM PC进行比较，指出它们在布局上的相似性，并提到Amiga 3000的设计对后来机器的影响。
• [pinewurst] 再次纠正关于SGI Indigo和早期Alphastation使用VME总线的误解，确认它们分别使用GIO32和Turbochannel总线。
• [whartung] 讨论HP 9000 712与NeXTStation的比较，考虑其在耐用性、支持性和性能等方面的优劣。
• [sugarpimpdorsey] 指出，专有UNIX工作站的超高 proprietary 性质，使得像SGI这样的厂商能以高价出售其硬件，因为无法在普通硬件上运行IRIX。
• [toast0] 认为LPX桌面设计是一个好的设计，解释了其在扩展性和传统布局方面的优点，并提到设计的趋同现象。
• [weinzierl] 回顾了计算机从集成键盘和显示器到桌面机箱再到塔式机箱的演变过程，指出设计随着时间推移变得更小、更实用。
• [aoki] 提到90年代初PC时代的三大趋势（Pentium、PCI、多平台Windows NT），并指出许多厂商转向基于PC总线和组件的设计以提高成本竞争力。
• [amelius] 建议研究台湾计算机历史，以寻找一些设计和生产上的“缺失环节”。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是早期Alphastation是否使用VME总线，[drewg123]和[pinewurst]都明确指出其使用的是Turbochannel总线而非VME。
• 另一个讨论点是计算机设计的趋同演化现象，[hapless]和[toast0]都提到不同品牌和架构的计算机由于解决相同的设计问题而变得相似。
• [sugarpimpdorsey] 强调了专有UNIX工作站的商业模式和其高价的原因，与其他讨论中提到的硬件设计和生产成本形成对比。

data.title: Piano Keys
data.author: gametorch
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了钢琴白键和黑键宽度排列的问题。由于黑键宽度相同且白键前端宽度一致，后端宽度无法完全相同。文章提出了几种优化方案，以最小化白键后端宽度的最大差异。初始方案如设置不同宽度组合，达到最大差异为B/2、B/6、B/8等。最佳传统方案是"B/12方案"，最大差异仅为B/12。进一步放宽条件，允许黑键和白键前端宽度变化，提出一种单位划分法，将一个八度分为878472单位，优化后最大差异显著减小，白键为0.0181英寸，黑键为0.0127英寸。这种优化方案在实际制造中更精确，显著减少宽度差异。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：钢琴键盘设计的合理性及其改进建议

不同观点：
• NooneAtAll3认为键盘按钮的宽度设计不够直观，建议页面增加带有a-b-c-d标注的图片，以及显示按钮宽度的图片，以便更好地理解设计。
• prmph对问题本身表示困惑，认为即使将黑键放在白键后面，且只占据白键宽度的一小部分，也不会影响弹奏，因为钢琴演奏者不会按压白键的末端。他质疑是否真的存在设计问题。
• bruce343434提供了自己 acoustic 钢琴的实际例子，指出黑键和白键后端的宽度是一样的，通过调整黑键的位置来实现，而不是将黑键置于白键正中间。
• ralfd表示对帖子的内容不理解，认为可能需要更多的图片来帮助理解。
• moefh支持一种传统的键盘布局方式，即通过黑键将八度音阶划分为两个部分，并通过实际观察自己周围的键盘，认为这种布局是普遍存在的。不过，他指出文章中的图片与实际布局不符，D键周围的黑键间距不正确。
• ajuc则从演奏角度提出根本性的质疑，认为现有钢琴键盘设计不规则，导致演奏者需要记住不同调上的和弦形状，建议将键盘设计为12个键（6白6黑），以简化和弦记忆和演奏。

补充讨论：
• 评论中存在关于键盘布局是否合理的争议，部分人认为现有设计有其历史和实际原因，而另一些人则提出改进建议，试图简化键盘布局以便于学习和演奏。
• 图片的需求在多个评论中被提及，表明视觉说明对理解键盘设计问题的重要性。
• 不同键盘（如acoustic钢琴与数字钢琴）之间的实际设计差异也被提及，增加了讨论的复杂性。

44576183.article_content:
Piano Keys
If you've ever looked closely at a piano keyboard you may have
noticed that the widths of the white keys are not all the same
at the back ends (where they pass between the black keys).  Of
course, if you think about it for a minute, it's clear they
couldn't possibly all be the same width, assuming the black keys
are all identical (with non-zero width) and the white keys all
have equal widths at the front ends, because the only simultaneous
solution of 3W=3w+2b and 4W=4w+3b is with b=0.
After realizing this I started noticing different pianos and how
they accommodate this little problem in linear programming.  Let W
denote the widths of the white keys at the front, and let B denote
the widths of the black keys.  Then let a, b,..., g (assigned to
their musical equivalents) denote the widths of the white keys
at the back.  Assuming a perfect fit, it's impossible to have
a = b = ... = g.  The best we can do is try to minimize the
greatest difference between any two of these keys.
One crude approach would be to set d=g=a=(W-B) and b=c=e=f=(W-B/2),
which gives a maximum difference of B/2 between the widths of any
two white keys (at the back ends).  This isn't a very good solution,
and I've never seen an actual keyboard based on this pattern
(although some cartoon pianos seem to have this pattern).  A better
solution is to set a=b=c=e=f=g=(W-3B/4) and d=(W-B/2).  With this
arrangement, all but one of the white keys have the same width at
the back end, and the discrepancy of the "odd" key (the key of "d")
is only B/4.  Some actual keyboards (e.g., the Roland HP-70) use
this pattern.
Another solution is to set c=d=e=f=b=(W-2B/3) and g=a=(W-5B/6),
which results in a maximum discrepancy of just B/6.  There are
several other combinations that give this same maximum discrepancy,
and actual keyboards based on this pattern are not uncommon.
If we set c=e=(W-5B/8) and a=b=d=f=g=(W-3B/4) we have a maximum
discrepancy of only B/8, and quite a few actual pianos use this
pattern as well.  However, the absolute optimum arrangement is to
set c=d=e=(W-2B/3) and f=g=a=b=(W-3B/4), which gives a maximum
discrepancy of just B/12.  This pattern is used on many keyboards,
e.g. the Roland PC-100.
The "B/12 solution" is the best possible given that all the black keys
are identical and all the white keys have equal widths at the front
ends.  For practical manufacturing purposes this is probably the
best approach.  However, suppose we relax those conditions and allow
variations in the widths of the black keys and in the widths of the
white keys at the front ends.  All we require is that the black
keys (in total) are allocated 5/12 of the octave.  On this basis,
what is the optimum arrangement, minimizing the maximum discrepancy
between any two widths of the same type?
Let A, B,...G denote the front-end widths of the white keys, and
let a#, c#, d#, f#, g# denote the widths of the black keys.  I
believe the optimum arrangement is given by dividing the octave
into 878472 units, and then setting
f=g=a=b=72156 units      c=d=e=74606 units      discrepancy=2450
f#=g#=a#=72520 units     c#=d#=74235 units      discrepancy=1715
F=G=A=B=126546 units     C=D=E=124096 units     discrepancy=2450
The maximum discrepancy between any two widths of the same class is
1/29.88 of the width of the average black key, which is less than
half the discrepancy for the "B/12 solution".
The max discrepancy is 1/358.56 of the total octave for the white
keys, and 1/512.22 for the black keys.  Since an octave is normally
about 6.5 inches, the max discrepancy is about 0.0181 inches for the
white keys and 0.0127 inches for the black keys.  (One peculiar fact
about this optimum arrangement is that the median point of the octave,
the boundary between f and f#, is exactly 444444 units up from the
start of the octave.)

data.title: The tech that the US Post Office gave us
data.article_summary: 美国邮政局在过去250年中悄然推动了多项技术创新。1918年，邮政局引入航空邮件服务，利用一战剩余飞机开辟了商业航空的先河，并为现代航空业奠定基础，如美国航空和联合航空的诞生。邮政局还试验了导弹邮递，但未成功。在地面处理方面，邮政局从20世纪20年代开始试验邮件取消机，到50年代部署机电分拣机，如Transorma信件分拣机。为应对二战后邮件量的激增，1963年推出了邮政编码系统，极大提高了分拣效率。邮政局通过这些技术创新，成为推动技术变革的重要力量。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国邮政服务（USPS）相关的技术创新及其影响

不同观点：
• **drewg123** 提到其在80年代末和90年代初的大学参与了USPS的手写识别技术开发，该项目获得了大量资助，甚至雇佣本科生参与研究。他强调了当时计算资源的稀缺和重要性，特别是与现代设备相比的差距。

• **voxadam** 补充了关于USPS光学字符识别（OCR）技术的细节，引用了90年代使用多台200 MHz Pentium Pro系统实现高速识别的例子。他认为，这些曾经的“强大计算能力”在今天看来已经过时，现代设备如Raspberry Pi可以轻松超越。

• **VWWHFSfQ** 赞赏USPS的“ informed Delivery”计划，该计划通过邮件发送即将到达的包裹图片，提升了用户体验。他还提到USPS手写识别技术目前已达到近98%的准确率，并讨论了USPS现代化计划及其面临的争议，如邮票价格上涨和服务中断问题。

• **botro** 强调USPS对多个行业和公司的历史性贡献，包括航空业、机器学习、Netflix和Amazon。他指出，USPS不仅推动了早期航空业的发展，还通过其数据集和物流支持促成了机器学习和电商巨头的崛起。

• **beanjuiceII** 对USPS的创新步伐放缓表示遗憾，批评企业官僚主义阻碍了持续创新。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是USPS现代化计划的成效和其对消费者的影响，尤其是邮票价格上涨和服务中断问题。
• 另一个值得注意的点是USPS的历史性技术贡献，如手写识别数据集对机器学习发展的推动作用。
• 评论中也涉及到技术进步的速度和现代计算资源的可及性，强调了技术更新换代对历史项目的超越。

这些观点展示了USPS在技术创新及其广泛影响方面的多面性，同时也反映了对其现代化进程中挑战的不同看法。

Report
/
AI
/
Tech
The tech that the US Post Office gave us
For 250 years, the agency quietly led the way for commercial aviation, optical character recognition, and more.
by
Emma Roth
Jul 19, 2025, 3:00 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
Image: The Verge / Collection of United States Postal Service
Emma Roth
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.
When you crack open your mailbox, it’s almost as if your letters just
appear
. Long before the days of speedy, overnight mail deliveries, postal service workers meticulously sorted through letters by hand and transported mail on horseback. For more than 250 years, the US Postal Service has worked behind the scenes to build a faster delivery network, and this mission has quietly pushed it to the forefront of technology.
“Most people treat the Postal Service like a black box,” USPS spokesperson Jim McKean tells
The Verge
. “You take your letter, you put it in a mailbox, and then it shows up somewhere in a couple of days. The truth is that that piece of mail gets touched by a lot of people and machines and transported in that period of time — it’s a modern marvel.”
One of its big breakthroughs took place in 1918 with the
introduction of airmail
. The USPS worked with the Army Signal Corps to
use leftover World War I aircraft
to launch the service, and the planes were as barebones as they could get. An excerpt from
a 1968 issue of
Postal Life
called the early aircraft “a nervous collection of whistling wires” with “linen stretched over wooden ribs, all attached to a wheezy, water-cooled engine.”
JR-1B mail planes were the first used by the USPS (1918).
Photo: National Archives and Records Administration
At the time, pilots literally risked their lives delivering mail — 34 of them died between 1918 and 1927. “There was no commercial aviation, no airports. There was no radio. There was no navigation,” USPS historian Stephen Kochersperger says. “The Postal Service had to develop all of those things just for getting the mail delivered.”
Once the USPS established that it could reliably deliver mail by plane, Congress allowed it to contract airmail service to commercial aviation companies, laying the groundwork for the major airlines that we know today,
like American Airlines
and
United Airlines
. Along with getting paid for delivering mail, contractors found that they could make even more money by carrying passengers with their cargo. “That was where commercial aviation took off,” Kochersperger says.
Airmail routes gradually began to expand internationally, first to Canada and then to Cuba. But a couple decades later, the USPS experimented with a novel form of delivery: mail-by-missile. In 1959, the USPS and the US Navy loaded a Regulus I missile
with two mail containers
that had 3,000 letters in total. The missile traveled 100 miles in around 23 minutes, successfully landing at a Navy base in Mayport, Florida, with the help of a parachute. Despite its success, the idea never took off. It turns out missiles just can’t carry that much mail. And overall, this rather ridiculous demonstration was more of a stunt to show force during the Cold War,
according to the Smithsonian
.
The Regulus I missle carried 3,000 pieces of mail (1959).
Photo: Collection of United States Postal Service
Back on the ground, the USPS set its sights on improving the speed of mail processing. Though it began experimenting with a mail canceling machine in the 1920s, which put a mark on used postage, it wasn’t until the 1950s that it deployed an electromechanical sorting machine. Instead of manually sorting mail
using the “pigeonhole” method
, in which workers would insert pieces of mail into different compartments inside the post office depending on the address, the machine could do that for them.
“The Postal Service is a driver of technological change.”
The
Transorma multi-position letter sorting machine

am-i-vibing
Detect agentic coding environments and AI assistant tools. This library allows CLI tools and Node apps to detect when they're being executed by AI agents. This enables them to adapt by, for example, providing different output formats or logs.
Installation
Install as library:
npm install am-i-vibing
Run as CLI tool:

Environment Types
The library detects three main types of environments:
Agent
: Command was directly run by an AI agent (e.g. Claude Code, Codex CLI, Jules)
Interactive
: Interactive commands run inside an AI environment (e.g. Cursor terminal, Replit shell)
Hybrid
: Environments that combine both agentic and interactive features in the same session (e.g. Warp)

data.title: What the Fuck Python
data.author: sundarurfriend
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Python语言的设计选择、行为特性以及其在实际应用中的合理性。

不同观点：
• harrisi认为Python中的这些特性和行为是有趣且值得探索的，尤其是对于学习解释型语言的运行机制有帮助。他提到CPython中确实存在实际的bug，但并不认为每个Python程序员都需要了解所有细节，只需团队中有人了解即可。

• pansa2指出了Python中`x += y`和`x = x + y`行为不一致的问题，并通过代码示例展示了这种不一致性所导致的困惑，包括元组和列表的不同处理方式。

• hansvm认为Python中关于对象身份比较和运算符使用的设计虽然有些奇怪，但在其他语言中也有类似问题。他还提到编译型语言中也有类似的优化行为，因此Python并不是唯一存在这种“特性”的语言。

• alabhyajindal支持对Python的批评，认为每种语言都有其设计缺陷，不应只针对JavaScript。

• Danjoe4强烈反对使用Python时过度关注语言的实现细节，认为良好的Python代码应遵循PEP8和PEP20的规范，以可读性为优先，而不是追求一些不必要的技巧和细节。

• LPisGood认为一些例子是在超出规范使用Python，误解了布尔表达式，并因此产生了不必要的困惑。

• procaryote认为Python在处理`is`和`==`的选择上是合理的，并质疑是否真的存在值得大惊小怪的问题，同时对比了Java中的类似问题。

• g42gregory讨论了Python中整数对象的回收和重用行为，认为这是解释器的实现细节，可能导致一些未定义的行为。

• ssalazar指出混淆引用相等和值相等是新手常犯的错误，并认为这样做会导致问题。

• globalnode提到Python中某些编程方式需要大量的心智负担，建议在代码可读性和注释之间找到平衡。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论提到了对Python的批评和防御态度，例如alabhyajindal对JavaScript的批评以及hislaziness对类似C语言书籍的喜爱。
• 有人提到Hacker News的标题自动转换功能（sundarurfriend）以及对Jupyter Notebooks的批评（rr808）。
• 评论中还出现了对ASCII标准的意外讨论（pyuser583）。

争议焦点：Python语言特性和行为的合理性以及在实际编程中应如何处理这些问题。一方认为这些特性是有趣且值得探索的，另一方则认为这些是误用或不必要的复杂性，应遵循最佳实践以提高代码可读性。

data.author: gandem
data.article_summary: 文章主要讲述了在升级到Go 1.24版本后，作者的团队发现服务内存使用量意外增加了约20%。尽管Go 1.24本应通过新的"Swiss Tables"特性减少内存和CPU开销，但升级后系统级指标显示内存增加，而Go运行时指标却没有变化。团队通过排查主要更新、深入分析系统级内存指标，发现问题在于虚拟内存更多地被提交到物理内存，导致系统指标与Go运行时指标不一致。最终，团队确认问题根源是运行时 refactor 引入的细微内存分配器回归问题，并与Go团队合作确认了原因。文章还预告下篇将介绍如何利用Go 1.24的"Swiss Tables"显著减少内存使用。

主要讨论点：CPU缓存和内存布局对数据查找性能的影响，特别是针对键值对存储结构的优化以及现代数据结构的学习资源。

不同观点：
• [dh2022] 认为当前的桶内存布局（[k1,v1],[k2,v2],[k3,v3]）在迭代查找时，由于每个键值对的大小接近CPU缓存行的大小（64字节），导致每次迭代都需要从RAM中获取数据，降低了性能。他提出了一种替代布局，即先存储所有键，再存储所有值（k1,k2,k3,...,v1,v2,v3），认为这种布局可以在查找时将多个键加载到缓存中，从而提高迭代速度。不过他也指出了这种方法的缺点，即如果查找的键通常是桶中的第一个键，那么当前的布局可能更好，因为键值对都在同一个缓存行中。

• [neuroelectron] 对[dh2022]的评论表示赞赏，但没有提出技术性意见，而是表达了对以前工作的怀念。

• [nitinreddy88] 对讨论的优化问题兴趣不大，更关注于学习现代数据结构（如Swiss tables）的实现，尤其是那些利用现代硬件特性（如SIMD）进行优化的数据结构。他询问了学习这些现代数据结构的最佳资源。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于两种内存布局的性能权衡。[dh2022]提出的替代布局在查找性能上可能更优，但其缺点是如果查找通常命中桶中的第一个键，则当前布局更好。这涉及到具体应用场景的选择和权衡。
• [nitinreddy88] 提出了对现代数据结构实现的学习需求，特别是那些利用现代硬件特性的数据结构，这是一个值得进一步讨论的方向。

总结：评论主要讨论了内存布局对性能的影响以及现代数据结构的学习资源。不同的观点集中在内存布局的性能权衡以及学习资源的推荐上。

When Go 1.24 was released in early 2025, we were eager to roll it out across our services. The headline featureâthe new
Swiss Tables
map implementationâpromised reduced CPU and memory overhead.
Our story begins while the new version was being rolled out internally. Shortly after deploying it to one of our data-processing services, we noticed an unexpected memory usage increase:
Close dialog
We observed the same pattern, a
~20% increase in memory usage
, across multiple environments before pausing the rollout. To confirm our suspicions, we conducted a bisect in the staging environment, which pointed directly to the Go 1.24 upgrade as the culprit.
But here's where things got truly puzzling: The increased memory usage wasn't showing up in Go runtime metrics and live heap profiles, which meant that, from the Go runtime's perspective, the service wasn't using more memory. This caught our attention immediately. After all, Go 1.24 was supposed to reduce memory usage thanks to Swiss Tables, not increase it.
In this two-part series, we'll share how we investigated this surprising increase and how the same release ultimately helped us
reduce
our memory footprint.
In this first post, we'll walk through how we diagnosed a subtle memory allocator regression introduced by a runtime refactor and how we worked with the Go team to identify and confirm the root cause. In
Part 2: How Go 1.24's Swiss Tables saved us hundreds of gigabytes
, we'll show how Go 1.24's new Swiss Tables implementation dramatically reduced the memory usage of a large in-memory mapâyielding a net win across our highest traffic services.
Ruling out major runtime changes in Go 1.24
Before diving deeper, we needed to eliminate the most likely suspects. Go 1.24 introduced a couple of  major changes that could potentially impact memory usage, so we systematically tested each one:
Swiss Tables
: This feature was supposed to reduce memory usage, but we needed to verify it wasn't somehow causing our problem. We created a test build with Swiss Tables disabled by setting the
GOEXPERIMENT=noswissmap
flag
. However,
this did not show any improvement in memory usage
.
Spin bit mutex
: This modified the internal implementation of the runtime mutexes. We also tested reverting the spin bit mutex implementation by creating a build with the
GOEXPERIMENT=nospinbitmutex
flag
. However,
we still observed the increased memory usage
with this Go experiment flag set.
Why system metrics disagreed with Go's runtime accounting
After ruling out the most likely culprits, we decided to deep dive into Go's runtime metrics to understand what was happening under the hood. These metrics provide valuable insights into Go's runtime, including internal memory managementâheap allocations, garbage collector (GC) cycles, and so on. Since Go 1.16, these metrics are exposed by the
runtime/metrics package
. For more details on Go runtime memory metrics, check out
Go memory metrics demystified
.
Despite the visible increase in overall memory usage, Go's runtime metrics showed almost no change after upgrading to version 1.24:
Close dialog
This contradiction was our first significant clue. If Go's internal accounting showed stable memory usage, why were system metrics telling a different story? System componentsâfor example, the Linux OOM Killerâwill use variants of these system metrics to control resource usage, such as Kubernetes memory limits, so it's important to understand why we see this discrepancy.
Digging deeper into system-level metrics revealed a substantial increase in
resident set size (RSS)
:
Close dialog
RSS measures
actual physical memory usage
in RAM, while Go's runtime metrics primarily track
virtual memory
âthe address space allocated to the process, which can be larger than physical RAM usage.
Our theory: More virtual memory committed to physical RAM
Go 1.24 wasn't requesting additional memory from the system, but something in the new version was causing previously uncommitted virtual memoryâmemory that was allocated but not yet physically usedâto be committed to physical RAM. This would explain why Go's internal memory accounting remained stable, while system-level RSS measurements showed increased memory consumption.
Was this affecting all memory regions allocated by Go, or just specific ones?
To answer this question, we turned to Linux's
/proc
filesystemâspecifically
/proc/[pid]/smaps
, which
provides detailed memory mapping information
for each process. This file shows exactly how much virtual memory is allocated and how much physical memory is used across different regions of a process's address space, giving us the microscopic view we needed.

data from a Go 1.24 process, w

data.title: 'Universal cancer vaccine' trains the immune system to kill any tumor
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种由佛罗里达大学科学家开发的实验性mRNA疫苗，这种疫苗通过增强免疫系统来对抗各种类型的肿瘤，有望成为一种“通用癌症疫苗”。与传统的个性化治疗不同，该疫苗不针对特定癌症，而是通过刺激免疫反应使肿瘤更易被免疫细胞识别和攻击，甚至对药物耐受的肿瘤也有效。这种疫苗利用脂质纳米颗粒传递mRNA，类似于新冠疫苗的机制，但目标是激发免疫系统攻击肿瘤细胞中的PD-L1蛋白。尽管仍在临床前研究阶段，该疫苗展示了广泛应用于多种癌症治疗的潜力，可能彻底改变癌症免疫疗法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于癌症研究进展的新闻报道及其影响

不同观点：
• 支持继续发布研究结果：[taylodl]认为，尽管许多头条报道可能夸大其词，但持续的研究和发表是推动癌症预防、检测和治疗进步的关键。他以乳腺癌和肺癌的治疗进展为例，强调了研究的重要性，即使大部分研究可能无果而终，但部分研究确实能挽救生命。

• 关注具体机制和实验细节：[asdff]从专业角度讨论了IFN-1和PD-L1抑制剂在肿瘤免疫反应中的作用机制，提出了一些尚未解答的问题，如PD-L1抑制剂如何在特定肿瘤中发挥作用。他还建议通过进一步实验，如单细胞RNA测序，来解答这些问题。

• 对研究成果持谨慎态度：[rpdillon]对研究成果表示了初步的怀疑，并提到需要注意研究是在小鼠模型中进行的。他引用了原始论文的摘要，强调了研究结果在小鼠中的有效性，但未提及人类临床应用。

• 对头条报道的反感：[phtrivier]强烈反对那些夸大其词的癌症新闻标题，认为这些报道是一种获取资金的手段，但对失去亲人的家属是一种侮辱。他呼吁等到真正治愈方法出现时再报道，而不是在每个小进展时都制造噱头。

• 对小鼠实验结果的怀疑：[0xbadc0de5]对研究成果在小鼠中的有效性表示鼓励，但提醒说许多在小鼠中有效的治疗方法在人类中并不奏效，主张保持 pragmatism（务实态度）。

补充讨论：
• 对高烧等副作用的关注：[SoftTalker]担心刺激免疫系统的治疗方法可能会导致高烧等副作用，但在报道中未提及这一点。

• 对mRNA研究经费削减的担忧：[3eb7988a1663]提到mRNA研究的经费被削减，暗示这对癌症研究的进展可能产生不利影响。

• 对科学研究伦理的质疑：[suzzer99]将研究与电影《我是传奇》的情节类比，表达了对科学家进行高风险实验的担忧。

争议焦点：
• 关于癌症研究新闻报道的真实性和伦理问题：一部分人认为头条报道夸大其词，对患者和家属不尊重；另一部分人认为持续的研究和报道是推动进步的必要手段。
• 小鼠实验结果的有效性：对在小鼠模型中取得的进展是否能在人类身上实现存在争议。

Following on from their breakthrough human trial that successfully reprogrammed the immune system to overpower glioblastoma, an aggressive brain tumor, the same scientists have now further developed the mRNA vaccine to fight not one but any cancer. It has the potential to do away with chemotherapy, surgery and radiation treatment.
University of Florida (UF) scientists have developed an experimental vaccine that dramatically boosts the immune system’s ability to fight tumors – even without targeting a specific cancer type. This "general purpose" mRNA jab works in a similar way to a Covid-19 vaccine but with a different target; it instructs the body's immune cells to rally and hit any kind of tumor in the same way they would attack a viral spike protein.
“This paper describes a very unexpected and exciting observation: that even a vaccine not specific to any particular tumor or virus – so long as it is an mRNA vaccine – could lead to tumor-specific effects,” said Elias Sayour, a pediatric oncologist and principal investigator at the RNA Engineering Laboratory at UF. “This finding is a proof of concept that these vaccines potentially could be commercialized as universal cancer vaccines to sensitize the immune system against a patient’s individual tumor."
Sayour has spent a decade working to harness the power of mRNA science in order to effectively treat cancer. The success with the
glioblastoma study
led to broadening the treatment's scope, not targeting one kind of tumor but instead focusing on giving the body's immune system the tools to fight any kind of cancer cell. It's part of a
growing body of evidence
that suggests mRNA vaccines might be a serious weapon in fighting the disease.
While the formulation isn't unlike the Covid-19 vaccine, which uses lipid nanoparticles to deliver the genetic instructions to the body, it is still somewhat different. Instead of the drug encoding a virus protein, it sends a message to the immune system to rally the troops. It essentially tells the body to produce certain proteins that stimulate the immune system – including a protein within cancer cells known as PD-L1 (Programmed Death-Ligand 1), which makes tumors become more visible to immune cells.
The researchers found a way to induce PD-L1 expression inside tumors using a generalized mRNA vaccine, essentially tricking the cancer cell into exposing itself, so immunotherapy can be more effective.
In this study on mice with melanoma, the vaccine was able to clear existing tumors that had proven drug-resistant. In other cancer models, including brain, skin and bone, the drug was even able to wipe out tumors without the assistance of any other treatment.
This approach is a little unorthodox in a field moving increasingly more towards personalized medicine with a precise target in the crosshairs. Previous research has focused more on homing in on a target or tailoring a vaccine specific to a patient's own cancer profile.
"This study suggests a third emerging paradigm," said study co-author Duane Mitchell, MD. "What we found is by using a vaccine designed not to target cancer specifically but rather to stimulate a strong immunologic response, we could elicit a very strong anticancer reaction. And so this has significant potential to be broadly used across cancer patients – even possibly leading us to an off-the-shelf cancer vaccine."
Scientists first discovered how mRNA "instruction manuals" could stimulate immune cells (in mice) in 1993, but a major hurdle has been working out how to deliver them into the body effectively. Around a decade ago, a breakthrough came when researchers found that lipid nanoparticles could effectively transport the incredibly fragile mRNA into the body without it being broken down in the bloodstream.
Now, the technology has rapidly advanced, in part due to the development of Covid-19 vaccines.
This study marks a key moment in cancer immunotherapy, demonstrating how a generalized, off-the-shelf mRNA vaccine – not tailored to any specific cancer tumor – can awaken the immune system and amplify the effects of existing treatments. By exposing well-hidden tumors by ramping up PD-L1 expression, the researchers have uncovered a new pathway that could transform how we prime the body to fight cancer.
While the vaccine is still being tested in pre-clinical anima studies, this work lays the foundation for a universal cancer vaccine strategy – one that doesn’t rely on customizing treatment specific to each patient but instead teaches the immune system how to fight smarter.

data.title: Linux and Secure Boot certificate expiration
data.author: pabs3
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了Linux系统中与安全启动（Secure Boot）相关的证书即将过期的问题。当前，许多Linux发行版使用由微软2011年签署的密钥来启动shim第一阶段引导程序，该密钥将于2025年9月11日到期。之后，若未更新shim并使用微软2023年的UEFI密钥进行签署，安装介质将无法在启用安全启动的系统上引导。

尽管已安装的系统可以通过自有密钥继续引导，但新安装或更新可能受到影响。硬件厂商需通过固件更新添加新密钥，而Linux发行版可以使用fwupd等工具来协助完成此更新。虽然可能会有一些问题，但操作系统厂商和维护者应能缓解大部分潜在风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：安全启动（Secure Boot）机制中的证书过期问题及其影响

不同观点：
• **londons_explore** 认为，不应该使用当前日期来检查那些可能不会更新的设备的证书有效性。相反，应根据固件编译时的日期来判断证书是否有效，这样可以避免时间变化导致的意外行为。

• **mkj** 指出，不仅仅是Linux系统受影响，Windows系统的证书在2026年也会过期。他认为证书设置过期日期可能只是为了防止签名密钥被泄露，但15年的等待时间过长，作用有限。同时提到微软的新证书将在2038年到期。

• **kragen** 对微软控制Linux启动证书表示不满，认为微软可以通过不作为来阻止用户启动Linux系统，并回顾了微软过去对Linux和Samba的法律威胁。

• **max-privatevoid** 强调，使用微软的密钥进行安全启动并不是真正的安全启动，而是“微软决定你能启动什么”。他认为应该采用用户自定义密钥的方式。

• **greatgib** 认为，必须通过微软来签名以在第三方电脑上运行操作系统是荒谬的，且微软轻易地取得了胜利，未曾受到严重挑战。

• **jeroenhd** 描述了联想笔记本在处理Nvidia固件和安全启动密钥上的问题，指出用户无法进入UEFI界面更改设置，且官方解决方案会在证书过期后失效。

• **LocalH** 从道德角度反对微软在Linux启动过程中发挥作用，认为任何由微软签名的密钥都不应在Linux启动中使用。

• **hcfman** 质疑向欧洲出售计算资源时由美国公司控制人工过期日期的合法性。

• **cm2187** 指出，现代操作系统中证书无处不在，这些证书可能是硬件设备的定时炸弹，尤其是ATM、医疗设备、智能家居和汽车等。

• **saidinesh5** 分享了个人经验，指出由于Nvidia驱动和虚拟机模块问题，不得不禁用安全启动，特别是在Arch系发行版上。

• **jacquesm** 提出了一种临时解决方案，建议通过断网、调整BIOS时钟等方式绕过证书过期问题。

• **laserbeam** 呼吁文章应包括简单明确的方法，让用户测试自己是否受此问题影响。

• **jmclnx** 表示一直避免使用安全启动，并预计许多新手Linux用户将在2025年9月后遇到问题。

• **1970-01-01** 回顾了BIOS的简单性，认为当前的证书过期问题只是众多UEFI和安全启动实现中的一个小问题，但可能带来系统修复或变砖的风险。

- 证书过期对不同系统和设备的影响，包括Windows和Linux。
- 微软在安全启动机制中的主导地位引发的争议和用户不满。
- 用户在实际操作中遇到的困难和临时解决方案。

[LWN subscriber-only content]
Welcome to LWN.net
The following subscription-only content has been made available to you
by an LWN subscriber.  Thousands of subscribers depend on LWN for the
best news from the Linux and free software communities.  If you enjoy this
article, please consider
subscribing to LWN
.  Thank you
for visiting LWN.net!
By
Jake Edge
July 16, 2025
Linux users who have
Secure Boot
enabled on their systems knowingly or unknowingly rely on a key from
Microsoft that is set to expire in September.  After that point, Microsoft
will no longer use that key to sign the
shim
first-stage UEFI bootloader that is used by Linux distributions to boot the
kernel with Secure Boot.  But the replacement key, which has been available
since 2023, may not be installed on many systems; worse yet, it may require
the hardware vendor to issue an update for the system firmware, which may
or may not happen.  It seems that the vast majority of systems will not be
lost in the shuffle, but it may require extra work from distributors and
users.
Mateus Rodrigues Costa
raised
the issue
on the Fedora devel mailing list on July 8.  He had noticed a
warning that came with "
this month's Windows 11 cumulative
update
"; it talked about Secure Boot certificates that are scheduled to
expire starting in June 2026.  Those particular certificates
are separate from the one used for shim, which expires much sooner.  In any
case, the problem of certificate expiration is one that the Linux world
will need to tackle.
The situation is rather complicated.  Daniel P. Berrangé
pointed
to a
page
at the
Linux Vendor Firmware Service (LVFS) site
that describes it.  LVFS is the home of
fwupd
and other tools that are used to update system firmware from Linux.  LVFS
and fwupd are the subject of an
LWN article from 2020
.
There are multiple moving parts to the problem.  In order to do a Secure
Boot into the Linux kernel, the UEFI boot process requires the first-stage
bootloader to be signed with a key in the
firmware database that has not expired.  Those keys are contained in
certificates, which have other information, such as an
expiration date and signature(s). The certificate expiration should largely only be a problem
when installing a new distribution on a Secure Boot system; the shim that gets installed
will have distribution-specific keys and can act as the root of trust for
running other programs (e.g. GRUB) using
those keys.
Currently, shim is signed with a Microsoft key from 2011 that expires on
September 11.  Past that point, installation media will no longer boot
unless it has an updated shim that is signed with the Microsoft 2023 UEFI
key for third-parties (which is different than the specific key mentioned
in the Windows update).  Any installed distribution should have a
bootloader signed with its own key that will continue to boot.
But there are lots of systems out there with a firmware database that lacks
Microsoft's new key, some have both old and new keys, while
there are likely some that only have the new key and cannot Secure Boot Linux
installation media at all at this point.  Vendors can (and hopefully most
will) provide firmware updates that add the new key, and installation
media can be created with a shim signed by it, but those updates have to
be installed on systems.  That's where LVFS and fwupd come in.
LVFS is a repository of vendor-firmware updates of various sorts, which
fwupd and other tools can use to install the pieces that are needed
into the firmware from Linux.
Berrangé noted that older versions of fwupd were unable to solve all of
the problems, "
but recent releases
have been enhanced to handle the updates that Linux users will need
to see, which should mitigate the worst of the impact
".  There may
still be a bit of a bumpy ride, however: "
Users should be 'aware' of the potential for trouble,
but hopefully the worst of the 'worry' part is handled by the OS vendors
and maintainers.
"
LVFS creator and maintainer Richard Hughes
agreed
,
noting that there were various ways that people's systems would be able to
get updated Secure Boot functionality.  A full firmware update might be
provided by the vendor, which would (presumably) add the new database,
including the new Microsoft key.  Another avenue would be a "key exchange key"
(KEK) update, which is a vendor-specific key that is signed by the
Microsoft key; it can be used by fwupd to update the database with the new key.  But there are some
caveats:
The KEK updates are going out at ~98% success, and db update is ~99%
success -- but even 1% multiplied by millions of people is a fair few
failures to deploy -- the "failed to write efivarfs" thing. What fixes it
for some people is rebooting and cle

data.title: Why you should choose HTMX for your next web-based side project (2024)
data.author: kugurerdem
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了为何在侧边项目中选择HTMX而非传统的MPA或复杂的SPA。HTMX通过允许部分页面重载，使多页应用（MPA）具备类似单页应用（SPA）的现代用户体验，同时保持较低的开发复杂度和成本。MPA简单但因全页面刷新而显得笨重，SPA则能提供流畅的体验但开发复杂。HTMX作为一种低复杂度工具，帮助开发者快速、经济地构建现代 web 应用，已成为作者技术栈（HAM Stack）的核心部分。对于个人开发者而言，HTMX能有效降低时间和金钱成本，是侧边项目的理想选择。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HTMX的优缺点及其在现代web开发中的应用

不同观点：
• cjs_ac认为HTMX通过"一次请求，一次响应"的模式，简化了网络交互，使得页面加载更快，避免了在客户端运行JS来决定是否请求其他资源的复杂性。
• wibbly非常喜欢HTMX，认为它为小规模项目提供了低成本的交互性，且可以优雅地降级为普通网站，对所有用户都有利。
• rapnie提到Datastar项目，认为HTMX项目已经完成，没有新功能，而Datastar提供了更小、更快、更面向未来的解决方案，建议在选择HTMX时也考虑Datastar。
• tekkk对"HAM栈"这个术语感到不适，认为虽然可以利用无服务器后端来降低成本，但重用可信的样板代码可能是更快的选择。
• lvl155质疑浏览器中JS的使用，认为每隔几个月就出现的新框架是因为我们拒绝改变浏览器，HTML需要现代化的解决方案，但目前这些方案显得丑陋和过时。
• eric-p7宣传了自己的轻量级库Solarite，该库为原生web组件添加了反应性和本地样式。
• manchmalscott提到Phoenix LiveView也能解决类似问题，通过web socket发送轻量级事件消息，服务器只响应新的HTML。
• librasteve对HTMX带来的多语言服务器端开发机会表示赞赏，并提到了多个相关项目。
• AndrewKemendo表示对HTMX感兴趣，但承认对新框架缺乏了解，希望看到一些值得注意的例子。
• Finnucane质疑HTMX带来的用户体验是否真的更快，认为许多JS密集型网站也感觉缓慢笨拙。
• chistev建议如果用vanilla JS太麻烦，可以直接使用Svelte。
• ranger_danger指出HTMX缺乏自动解析JSON响应的功能，建议增加类似"hx-source"的属性以简化开发。
• MountainMan1312正在尝试将HTMX用于个人网站，结合知识库和版本控制功能，但对具体实现方式还在探索中。
• hungryhobbit认为HTMX像是一个寻找问题的解决方案，暗示其并非对所有项目都适用。

补充讨论：
• HTMX的优缺点：简化了网络交互，但可能缺乏一些现代功能。
• 其他类似解决方案：如Datastar和Phoenix LiveView，提供了不同的实现方式和功能。
• 新框架和技术的不断出现：反映了开发社区对浏览器和JS现状的不满，以及对更现代化、更高效解决方案的追求。
• 实际应用中的需求和挑战：如自动解析JSON响应的功能需求，以及在具体项目中的实用性探索。

Why you should choose HTMX for your next web-based side project - and ditch the crufty MPA and complex SPA
Date: 2024-02-23 |
create
|
hamstack
|
htmx
|
mpa
|
spa
|
tech
|
DISCLOSURE:
If you buy through affiliate links, I may earn a small commission.
(disclosures)
I build
a lot of side projects
so I'm always on the lookout for technologies and paradigms that allow me to build them faster and cheaper at a similar quality. For the last several months I've been experimenting with building web apps with
low-js tools like HTMX and Alpine
.
In this post I'll share why I think HTMX is a great choice for building web apps faster and cheaper and why it's now a core part of my tech stack -
The HAM Stack
.
MPA vs SPA
Multi-Page Apps (MPA)
In the beginning we had Multi-Page Apps (MPA).
Each URL goes to a web page
This web-page is rendered server-side and sent back to the user
If you need to update something on the page (because a user changes something or it needs to refresh) then the full page needs to reload
This works fine but it gives a very slow / clunky feel because you need to reload EVERYTHING any time one thing on the page changes. For an example of this - think of a State government website, most of those are still old-school MPAs and they feel old and clunky compared to most modern apps.
MPA Pros and Cons
Pros: Simple to build
Cons: Feels slow and clunky due to refreshes
Single-Page Apps (SPA)
To solve this, Single-Page Apps (SPA) were created.
A URL loads a large JS payload containing a bunch of app logic
This JS takes over page rendering
It uses internal state to determine what the page should look like and does data transfers behind the scenes so it only needs to update the parts of the page that need to change
This feels better to the user because changes feel faster. The page only updates where it needs to and we don't need a full page refresh to change data. Most apps / websites today feel like this because it generally provides a better user experience.
Pros: Rich "modern" user experiences
Cons: Complex at scale - dealing w data transfers (graphQL was built for this), abstractions, and app logic payload sizes
So in general:
Multi-Page Apps (MPA)
- Simple to build but hard to get rich "modern" user experiences
Single-Page Apps (SPA)
- Complex to build but can achieve rich "modern" user experiences
MPA vs HTMX vs SPA
Image inspiration from
u/Abhilash26 on r/htmx
.
HTMX has been around for several years but has really gained mass hype in the past year or so. The hype is not unfounded - it often allows you to
build modern web apps faster and cheaper than a SPA
.
HTMX essentially extends HTML so that it can do partial page reloads.
Any element can specify how it can retrieve up-to-date data and when it should do that
The element can then specify what to do with the new data - replacing itself or other elements on the page
If we look back at the MPA vs SPA comparison, we can see that the lack of partial page reloads is really the main thing holding MPAs back. So adding this capability into an MPA largely allows you to get most of the rich "modern" user experiences of a SPA with the complexity level of an MPA.
HTMX for Side Projects
The goal of a side project is often just to build the thing. You likely don't have a team of engineers or warchest of VC-money to do so - it's just you and your computer.
So lowering the cost of building - in time and money - is crucial to making a side project successful.
From my perspective, HTMX provides a great balance between allowing you to build modern apps with very low complexity (and thus time and money cost). Thus it's become a core part of my tech stack -
the HAM Stack
.

• cjs_ac认为HTMX通过"一次请求，一次响应"的模式，简化了网络交互，使得页面加载更快，避免了在客户端运行JS来决定是否请求其他资源的复杂性。
• wibbly非常喜欢HTMX，认为它为小规模项目提供了低成本的交互性，且可以优雅地降级为普通网站，对所有用户都有利。
• rapnie提到Datastar项目，认为HTMX项目已经完成，没有新功能，而Datastar提供了更小、更快、更面向未来的解决方案，建议在选择HTMX时也考虑Datastar。
• tekkk对"HAM栈"这个术语感到不适，认为虽然可以利用无服务器后端来降低成本，但重用可信的样板代码可能是更快的选择。
• lvl155质疑浏览器中JS的使用，认为每隔几个月就出现的新框架是因为我们拒绝改变浏览器，HTML需要现代化的解决方案，但目前这些方案显得丑陋和过时。
• eric-p7宣传了自己的轻量级库Solarite，该库为原生web组件添加了反应性和本地样式。
• manchmalscott提到Phoenix LiveView也能解决类似问题，通过web socket发送轻量级事件消息，服务器只响应新的HTML。
• librasteve对HTMX带来的多语言服务器端开发机会表示赞赏，并提到了多个相关项目。
• AndrewKemendo表示对HTMX感兴趣，但承认对新框架缺乏了解，希望看到一些值得注意的例子。
• Finnucane质疑HTMX带来的用户体验是否真的更快，认为许多JS密集型网站也感觉缓慢笨拙。
• chistev建议如果用vanilla JS太麻烦，可以直接使用Svelte。
• ranger_danger指出HTMX缺乏自动解析JSON响应的功能，建议增加类似"hx-source"的属性以简化开发。
• MountainMan1312正在尝试将HTMX用于个人网站，结合知识库和版本控制功能，但对具体实现方式还在探索中。
• hungryhobbit认为HTMX像是一个寻找问题的解决方案，暗示其并非对所有项目都适用。

补充讨论：
• HTMX的优缺点：简化了网络交互，但可能缺乏一些现代功能。
• 其他类似解决方案：如Datastar和Phoenix LiveView，提供了不同的实现方式和功能。
• 新框架和技术的不断出现：反映了开发社区对浏览器和JS现状的不满，以及对更现代化、更高效解决方案的追求。
• 实际应用中的需求和挑战：如自动解析JSON响应的功能需求，以及在具体项目中的实用性探索。

data.author: vFunct
data.article_summary: 本文提出了一种新框架，利用自回归语言模型的固有知识，实现多个后续词 token 的同时预测，从而提升推理速度和并行性。该方法包括：(1) 掩码输入模式，联合预测多个未来词；(2) 引入门控 LoRA 机制，保持原模型功能并支持多词预测；(3) 轻量级可学习采样模块，生成连贯序列；(4) 辅助训练损失，增强生成词的一致性和准确性；(5) 推测生成策略，实现词的二次扩展并保持高保真度。实验表明，该方法在预训练模型上通过有监督微调，显著加速文本生成，例如代码和数学任务提速近5倍，聊天和知识任务提速约2.5倍，且不损失质量。

View a PDF of the paper titled Your LLM Knows the Future: Uncovering Its Multi-Token Prediction Potential, by Mohammad Samragh and 6 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Autoregressive language models are constrained by their inherently sequential nature, generating one token at a time. This paradigm limits inference speed and parallelism, especially during later stages of generation when the direction and semantics of text are relatively certain. In this work, we propose a novel framework that leverages the inherent knowledge of vanilla autoregressive language models about future tokens, combining techniques to realize this potential and enable simultaneous prediction of multiple subsequent tokens. Our approach introduces several key innovations: (1) a masked-input formulation where multiple future tokens are jointly predicted from a common prefix; (2) a gated LoRA formulation that preserves the original LLM's functionality, while equipping it for multi-token prediction; (3) a lightweight, learnable sampler module that generates coherent sequences from the predicted future tokens; (4) a set of auxiliary training losses, including a consistency loss, to enhance the coherence and accuracy of jointly generated tokens; and (5) a speculative generation strategy that expands tokens quadratically in the future while maintaining high fidelity. Our method achieves significant speedups through supervised fine-tuning on pretrained models. For example, it generates code and math nearly 5x faster, and improves general chat and knowledge tasks by almost 2.5x. These gains come without any loss in quality.

主要讨论点：Google Maps等平台上的信息不准确问题及其背后的技术与管理难题

不同观点：
• abathur认为Google Maps上的商家描述不准确，例如某家本地酒吧的描述中提到的多项设施和提供的食物饮料并不存在。尽管已经有人反馈，但问题仍未解决。这导致了一些顾客的负面体验，如想要玩桌球或飞镖的顾客感到失望。
• jwr支持abathur的观点，并指出这不仅是信息概述的问题，而是Google整体的信息管理问题。他分享了自己多年与Google Maps错误信息斗争的经历，认为Google对反馈的响应不积极，且由于其规模庞大，可能并不重视这些不一致问题。
• jh00ker则关注当相关讨论被索引后可能带来的影响，提到"Dave Barry去世但仍在辩驳"的例子，暗示信息错误可能会引发更大的误解。
• ilaksh从技术角度分析了问题的原因，认为部分错误源于名称的混淆，尤其是当多个同名人物存在时。他建议通过增加默认问题（如"其他同名人物"）来改善，并讨论了Google知识图谱的潜在应用问题。
• ChrisMarshallNY表示对Google纠正错误不乐观，但赞赏Dave Barry的幽默回应，同时提到自己对Google长期存在的问题也有类似体验。
• rapind和ciconia的评论较为简短，前者提到AI生成内容可能导致诽谤问题，后者则用讽刺的方式表达对AI交流能力的失望。
• yalogin分享了与Meta AI互动的负面体验，指出一旦AI开始“幻觉”生成错误信息，就很难纠正。
• zaptrem和_ache_的评论则引发了对"Dave Barry"身份的幽默讨论，zaptrem提到另一个同名人物的死亡事件，而_ache_则用讽刺方式建议重新咨询医生。
• h2zizzle对Dave Barry表示支持，并表达了对当前AI和Google产品的不满，认为它们经常扭曲现实，且问题难以解决。
• devinplatt提到Wikipedia在敏感话题上的特别政策，暗示Google等平台可以从中学习管理经验。
• foobarbecue则以讽刺的方式建议只在不重要的事实任务中使用AI，如写推荐信或制定政策。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Google等平台信息不准确且难以修正的问题，用户反馈常常被忽视，导致错误信息长期存在。
• 技术上的讨论涉及AI生成内容的可靠性、名称混淆问题以及知识图谱的应用潜力。
• 评论中还提到了AI“幻觉”问题，即AI生成不准确或错误的信息且难以纠正，用户对此表示强烈不满。
• 部分评论带有幽默和讽刺性质，但也反映了用户对AI和大型科技公司产品现状的深刻不满。

data.title: Postgres to ClickHouse: Data Modeling Tips
data.author: saisrirampur
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了如何将PostgreSQL的数据通过Change Data Capture (CDC) 复制到ClickHouse，以实现事务工作负载和实时分析的分离。文章详细介绍了使用工具如PeerDB和ClickPipes实现CDC的过程，并深入探讨了在ClickHouse中进行数据建模和查询优化的最佳实践。

主要内容包括：
1. **数据复制机制**：通过PostgreSQL的逻辑解码（Logical Decoding）实现数据变更的捕捉和复制。
2. **ReplacingMergeTree引擎**：ClickHouse使用该引擎处理频繁的更新和删除操作，通过插入新版本的数据实现去重。
3. **数据建模策略**：包括数据去重、自定义排序键、优化JOIN操作、物化视图（Materialized Views）、反规范化（Denormalization）等。
4. **实际示例**：通过一个StackOverflow数据集展示同步过程，包括初始快照加载及后续的插入、更新、删除操作。

本文为之前版本的进阶版，适合希望利用ClickHouse进行分析的PostgreSQL用户参考。

Postgres to ClickHouse: Data Modeling Tips V2
Lionel Palacin & Sai Srirampur
Mar 6, 2025
-
26
minutes read
It is becoming increasingly
common
for customers to use Postgres and ClickHouse together, with Postgres powering transactional workloads and ClickHouse powering analytics. Each is a purpose-built database optimized for its respective workload. A common approach to integrating Postgres with ClickHouse is Change Data Capture (CDC). CDC continuously tracks inserts, updates, and deletes in Postgres and replicates them to ClickHouse, enabling real-time analytics.
You can implement Postgres CDC to ClickHouse using
PeerDB
, an open-source replication tool, or leverage a fully integrated experience in ClickHouse Cloud with
ClickPipes
.
Since Postgres and ClickHouse are different databases, an important aspect alongside replication is effectively modeling tables and queries in ClickHouse to maximize performance.
This blog takes a deep dive into how Postgres CDC to ClickHouse works internally and delves into best practices for data modeling and query tuning.
We will cover topics such as data deduplication strategies, handling custom ordering keys, optimizing JOINs, materialized views (MVs) including refreshable MVs, denormalization, and more.
You can also apply these learnings to one-time migrations (not CDC) from Postgres, so we expect this to help any Postgres users looking to use ClickHouse for analytics. We published a
v1
of this blog late last year; this one will be an advanced version of that blog.
Dataset
#
Throughout this blog post, we will illustrate the strategies using a real-world dataset, specifically a subset of the well-known StackOverflow dataset, which we will load into PostgreSQL. This dataset is used across ClickHouse documentation, and you can find more information about it
here
. We also implemented a Python script that simulates user activity on StackOverflow. Instructions on how to reproduce the experiments can be found on
GitHub
.
How does data get replicated?
#
PostgreSQL logical decoding
#
ClickPipes and PeerDB use
Postgres Logical Decoding
to consume changes as they happen in Postgres. The Logical Decoding process in Postgres enables clients like ClickPipes to receive changes in a human-readable format, i.e., a series of INSERTs, UPDATEs, and DELETEs. To learn more about how Logical Decoding works, you can read one of our
blogs
that goes into full detail.
As part of the replication process, ClickPipes automatically creates corresponding tables with the most
native data-type mapping
in ClickHouse and performs initial snapshots/backfills super
efficiently
.
ReplacingMergeTree
#
ClickPipes maps Postgres tables to ClickHouse using the
ReplacingMergeTree
engine. ClickHouse performs best with append-only workloads and
does not recommend
frequent UPDATEs. This is where ReplacingMergeTree is particularly powerful.
With ReplacingMergeTree, updates are modeled as inserts with a newer version (
_peerdb_version
) of the row, while deletes are inserts with a newer version and
_peerdb_is_deleted
marked as true. The ReplacingMergeTree engine in background deduplicates/merges data and retains the latest version of the row for a given primary key (id), enabling efficient handling of UPDATEs and DELETEs as versioned inserts.

Illustrative example
#
The illustration below walks through a basic example of synchronization of a table
users
between PostgreSQL and ClickHouse using ClickPipes.
Step 1
shows the initial snapshot of the 2 rows in PostgreSQL and ClickPipes performing the initial load of those 2 rows to ClickHouse. If you observe, both rows are copied as-is to ClickHouse.
Step 2
shows three operations on the users table: inserting a new row, updating an existing row, and deleting another row.
Step 3
shows how ClickPipes replicates the INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations to ClickHouse as versioned inserts. The UPDATE appears as a new version of the row with ID 2, while the DELETE appears as a new version of ID 1 with is _deleted marked as true. Because of this, ClickHouse has three additional rows compared to PostgreSQL.
As a result, running a simple query like
SELECT count(*) FROM users;
may produce different results in ClickHouse and PostgreSQL. According to the
ClickHouse merge documentation

本文讨论了如何将PostgreSQL的数据通过Change Data Capture (CDC) 复制到ClickHouse，以实现事务工作负载和实时分析的分离。文章详细介绍了使用工具如PeerDB和ClickPipes实现CDC的过程，并深入探讨了在ClickHouse中进行数据建模和查询优化的最佳实践。

主要内容包括：
1. **数据复制机制**：通过PostgreSQL的逻辑解码（Logical Decoding）实现数据变更的捕捉和复制。
2. **ReplacingMergeTree引擎**：ClickHouse使用该引擎处理频繁的更新和删除操作，通过插入新版本的数据实现去重。
3. **数据建模策略**：包括数据去重、自定义排序键、优化JOIN操作、物化视图（Materialized Views）、反规范化（Denormalization）等。
4. **实际示例**：通过一个StackOverflow数据集展示同步过程，包括初始快照加载及后续的插入、更新、删除操作。

本文为之前版本的进阶版，适合希望利用ClickHouse进行分析的PostgreSQL用户参考。

data.author: liquid99
data.article_summary: AMD即将于7月23日发售基于Zen 5架构的Ryzen Threadripper Pro 9000 WX系列CPU，最高端的Threadripper Pro 9995WX拥有96核192线程，售价高达11,699美元。该系列还包括其他型号：64核的9985WX售价7,999美元，32核的9975WX售价4,099美元，24核的9965WX售价2,899美元，以及24核的9955WX起售价1,649美元。这些处理器专为工作站设计，适用于专业渲染和本地AI部署，性能较前代有显著提升。Dell、HP、Lenovo和Supermicro等厂商也将推出搭载该系列芯片的高端工作站。非Pro版的Threadripper 9980X和9970X价格尚未公布，预计会更低。

AMD’s latest Zen 5-based Ryzen
Threadripper Pro 9000 WX-Series
of CPUs go on sale later this month, and the top option will be
priced at $11,699
. The 9000 WX-Series chips are designed for workstations, with the $11,699 Threadripper Pro 9995WX shipping on July 23rd with 96 cores and 192 threads.
Dell, HP, Lenovo, and Supermicro will all start selling high-end workstations with the latest Threadripper 9000 series of chips on July 23rd, and DIY builders will be able to purchase the processors through AMD’s channel partners.
AMD’s Threadripper Pro 9995WX looks like it will comfortably beat its previous generation chips.

All five processors are designed to be faster in professional rendering tools like Chaos V-Ray, or tools like Adobe After Effects.
The Pro 9000 WX-Series processors are also designed for local AI deployments, including fine-tuning models, inference, and AI application development. “When running a context-based prompting inference test using DeepSeek R1 32B, we are seeing a 49 percent better performance of Threadripper Pro 9000 over Intel,” claims AMD.
AMD hasn’t yet revealed pricing for its non-Pro
Threadripper 9980X and 9970X processors
, but expect those prices to be a lot less for DIY builders.

data.title: MIPS: The hyperactive history and legacy of the pioneering RISC architecture
data.author: rob_lh
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MIPS架构的历史、技术特点、衰落原因及其与竞争架构的比较

不同观点：
• **MIPS的成功与失败**：brucehoult认为MIPS在游戏机、网络设备和超级计算机等多个领域取得了显著成功，但最终由于SGI转向Itanium而放弃MIPS，导致其衰落。这表明MIPS的技术实力和市场潜力，但管理决策失误是其失败的主要原因。

• **MIPS架构的优点与缺点**：brucehoult指出MIPS架构设计经典且具有持久的价值，但也存在一些技术上的不足，例如延迟槽和条件分支需要多条指令，这相对于一些现代ISA（如ARM）显得不够高效。

• **MIPS与ARM的竞争**：brucehoult提到MIPS在引入混合指令集（如MIPS16和microMIPS）方面落后于ARM，总是处于跟随地位，缺乏领导力，这可能是其在与ARM竞争中失利的原因之一。

• **MIPS的未来与RISC-V的兴起**：brucehoult认为，设计和维护一个独立的ISA非常昂贵且困难，MIPS虽然推出了nanoMIPS，但为时已晚，无法与已经获得关注的RISC-V竞争。他希望MIPS的工程师能在RISC-V上取得成功。

补充讨论：
• **技术幽默与竞争**：DonHopkins分享了一个关于硬件设计师间的玩笑，提到MIPS可以支持大小端（SPIM），而SPARC的小端版本被戏称为CRAPS，这反映出当时技术人员之间的竞争和幽默文化。

争议焦点：
• **MIPS的衰落是由于技术原因还是管理决策**：brucehoult明确指出MIPS的衰落主要是因为SGI在Itanium上的错误决策，而不仅仅是因为技术上的不足。这暗示了管理决策在技术产品成败中的关键作用。

data.title: The borrowchecker is what I like the least about Rust
data.author: jakobnissen
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Rust语言中的借用检查器（borrow checker），这是Rust实现内存安全的核心机制，但也带来了不少人体工学问题。作者认为借用检查器被过度推崇，其在Rust安全性中的作用被夸大。借用检查器要求在编译时确定所有引用的生命周期，这一要求过于严格，导致许多合理的代码被拒绝。例如，当代码中同时存在多个指向不同字段的可变引用时，借用检查器会错误地拒绝这些代码。此外，借用检查器无法跨函数或在函数内的控制流之间进行有效推理，导致更多误报。作者指出，借用检查器的这些局限性给开发者带来了实际的困扰，尤其是在修改现有项目时。尽管小例子可以展示问题，但真正的痛苦往往在处理大型项目时才会显现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust语言的borrow checker（借用检查器）的优缺点及其对语言成功的影响

不同观点：
• eigenspace认为，borrow checker是Rust成功的重要原因。他指出，新语言很难成功，除非能展示出其他语言无法实现的功能。borrow checker提供了这种独特性，并吸引了特定的开发者文化。
• alilleybrinker解释了borrow checker在跨函数推理 borrowing（借用）方面的局限性，并提出了一些绕过这些限制的方法，如使用getter函数或直接访问公共字段。
• jltsiren分享了自己在Rust和C++之间的开发经验，指出在Rust中需要以Rust的方式编写代码，而不是将C++的思维方式带入Rust。他还提到使用索引在图/树实现中的好处。
• IshKebab强调borrow checker不仅限于内存安全，还能提高代码的正确性，因为它强制了一种树状所有权模式。
• Fraterkes指出，borrow checker的严格性在某些开发场景（如生态系统建设）中是有益的，但在其他场景（如游戏开发）中可能不合适，因为这些场景需要更大的灵活性。
• int_19h探讨了从Rust中提取一个不使用borrow checker的子集的可能性，并提出了使用宏和自定义标准库的方案。
• airstrike表示，虽然不喜欢borrow checker，但其他特性（如模式匹配、零成本抽象、类型系统、并发安全性等）使Rust仍然具有吸引力。
• umanwizard支持Rust的借用规则，认为它们对于确保代码正确性是必要的，并指出这些规则不仅仅是实现细节，而是Rust语言设计的核心部分。
• Animats指出Rust中的borrow checker在处理后向引用时的不足，并讨论了三种常见的工作around（使用索引、不安全代码、运行时检查），同时提出静态分析工具的可能解决方案。
• int08h对比了Rust和C++，认为C++中的元编程问题比Rust的借用检查问题更复杂和烦人。
• cibyr和isodev认为，borrow checker是Rust提供无垃圾收集语言中最好的解决方案，并且编译器帮助开发者识别潜在问题是Rust的一大优势。
• mirekrusin和dhbradshaw提到MoonBit和Gleam作为Rust的替代语言，它们没有borrow checker但具有类似的特性。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到Rust的borrow checker在某些场景下的局限性，如后向引用问题和跨函数推理问题。
• 一些开发者提出了绕过borrow checker限制的方法，如使用索引、不安全代码或运行时检查。
• 也有开发者支持borrow checker，认为它是Rust语言成功和代码正确性的关键因素。
• 探讨了Rust中可能的语言设计改进和工具支持，如静态分析和Polonius借用检查算法。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于borrow checker的严格性是否必要，以及它对开发效率和代码正确性的影响。一些开发者认为borrow checker过于严格，限制了开发的灵活性，而另一些开发者则认为它是Rust成功的核心，并确保了代码的正确性和安全性。

• alilleybrinker解释了borrow checker在跨函数推理 borrowing（借用）方面的局限性，并提出了一些绕过这些限制的方法，如使用getter函数或直接访问公共字段。
• jltsiren分享了自己在Rust和C++之间的开发经验，指出在Rust中需要以Rust的方式编写代码，而不是将C++的思维方式带入Rust。他还提到使用索引在图/树实现中的好处。
• IshKebab强调borrow checker不仅限于内存安全，还能提高代码的正确性，因为它强制了一种树状所有权模式。
• Fraterkes指出，borrow checker的严格性在某些开发场景（如生态系统建设）中是有益的，但在其他场景（如游戏开发）中可能不合适，因为这些场景需要更大的灵活性。
• int_19h探讨了从Rust中提取一个不使用borrow checker的子集的可能性，并提出了使用宏和自定义标准库的方案。
• airstrike表示，虽然不喜欢borrow checker，但其他特性（如模式匹配、零成本抽象、类型系统、并发安全性等）使Rust仍然具有吸引力。
• umanwizard支持Rust的借用规则，认为它们对于确保代码正确性是必要的，并指出这些规则不仅仅是实现细节，而是Rust语言设计的核心部分。
• Animats指出Rust中的borrow checker在处理后向引用时的不足，并讨论了三种常见的工作around（使用索引、不安全代码、运行时检查），同时提出静态分析工具的可能解决方案。
• int08h对比了Rust和C++，认为C++中的元编程问题比Rust的借用检查问题更复杂和烦人。
• cibyr和isodev认为，borrow checker是Rust提供无垃圾收集语言中最好的解决方案，并且编译器帮助开发者识别潜在问题是Rust的一大优势。
• mirekrusin和dhbradshaw提到MoonBit和Gleam作为Rust的替代语言，它们没有borrow checker但具有类似的特性。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到Rust的borrow checker在某些场景下的局限性，如后向引用问题和跨函数推理问题。
• 一些开发者提出了绕过borrow checker限制的方法，如使用索引、不安全代码或运行时检查。
• 也有开发者支持borrow checker，认为它是Rust语言成功和代码正确性的关键因素。
• 探讨了Rust中可能的语言设计改进和工具支持，如静态分析和Polonius借用检查算法。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于borrow checker的严格性是否必要，以及它对开发效率和代码正确性的影响。一些开发者认为borrow checker过于严格，限制了开发的灵活性，而另一些开发者则认为它是Rust成功的核心，并确保了代码的正确性和安全性。

data.title: Triggering QUIC
data.author: gm678
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了触发客户端使用QUIC传输协议的机制。传统方法是让应用尝试通过QUIC连接，若失败则回退到TCP。然而，这种方法可能导致延迟，特别是在网络不支持QUIC的情况下。为避免时间 penalty，服务器可在首次TCP/TLS连接中通过HTTP头字段（如`alt-svc`）向客户端表明其支持QUIC，使客户端在后续连接中使用QUIC。这种方法已在Chrome浏览器中使用多年。

此外，Apple的Safari浏览器通过DNS查询（使用SVCB记录和ALPN字段）直接确定服务器是否支持QUIC，从而触发QUIC连接。这意味着目前存在两种主要的QUIC触发机制：Chrome使用的“第二使用”方法和Safari依赖的DNS方法。

最后，文章提到衡量QUIC采用率的传统方法，即通过支持QUIC的服务统计其使用率。

44616754.article_content:
The ISP Column
A column on various things Internet
Other Formats:
Triggering QUIC
July 2025
Geoff Huston
Last month, in June 2025, I
reported
on our progress with the adoption of the QUIC transport protocol. Here I would like to look at the mechanisms used to trigger a client application (typically a browser) to connect to the server using the QUIC transport protocol.
A conventional way to introduce a new transport service is to let applications initiate a connection using the new service. If the connection is unresponsive, then the application can back off to use the old transport service. In the case of QUIC, this would be a QUIC connection request made via a UDP packet directed to the serverâs port 443, and if the client doesnât receive a response after some timeout interval it will fall back to TCP (and TLS) by sending a SYN packet to the serverâs TCP destination port 443.
This connection process can be slow, particularly if the server or the intervening network does not support QUIC transport. As the client isnât necessarily aware of the round-trip time to the server, the client would normally err on the side of caution and wait at this juncture for at least one or two seconds before abandoning the connection attempt. QUIC was designed to increase the responsiveness of services over the network, not to introduce new sources of delay. A client could could use a smaller timeout interval, but this would be prone to false signals, where the client falls back to TCP unnecessarily. A client could set up a âconnection raceâ, sending a QUIC connection packet and a TCP SYN packet, and follow through by completing the connection with the first protocol to respond, but this would impose additional load on the server as it is forced to set up two connection contexts for every client connection.
One way to establish if a QUIC connection is viable  without paying a time penalty is for the server to signal the capability to use QUIC to the client in the first (TCP/TLS) connection, allowing the client to initiate a QUIC session on the second and subsequent connections. This second-use approach is defined in an Internet standard for Alternative Services (
RFC 7838
), which is a means to list alternative ways to access the same resources, using the HTTP header fields.
For example,
alt-svc: quic=":443"; ma=2592000;
This indicates that the same material is accessible using QUIC over port 443. The âmaâ field is the time to keep this information cached in the local client (in seconds), which in this case is 30 days. The semantics of this header is that this is not an unconditional directive, and the client is free to ignore this information and continue with the existing TCP/TLS protocol choice.
However, itâs not quite as simple as it may sound. The HTTP protocol introduced the concept of session persistence in HTTP/1.0 so that the underlying transport session is kept open for some keepalive interval, allowing reuse of the TCP and TLS state without the overheads of establishing a new session. The implication for the second-use signaling approach was that the original HTTP session was kept open across multiple requests, indefinitely deferring any subsequent connection that would use the QUIC transport protocol.
This form of triggering the use of QUIC has been bundled into the Chrome browser for more than a decade.
When Apple introduced support for QUIC in its Safari browser they used a different trigger, namely the DNS. The IETF has introduced the SVCB record in the DNS, allowing a number of connection profile items to be stashed in the DNS (RFC 9460). SVCB records facilitate the discovery of alternative endpoints for a service, allowing clients to choose the most suitable endpoint based on their needs and capabilities. There is the HTTPS DNS record, which is the SVCB record for use for HTTPS service connections. Relevant here is the
Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation
(ALPN) field where the token h3 denotes a server capability to support QUIC (HTTP/3) (
RFC 9114
).
Safari browsers that support the use of QUIC will query the DNS for an HTTPS record, and if there is an alpn field that specifies h3 in this record, then the browser can immediately proceed with opening a QUIC connection to the server, based on the knowledge that the server has indicated that it can support QUIC connections.
This form of triggering the use of QUIC has been bundled into the Safari browser for more than a year.
This means that we have two triggers for the use of QUIC, one as a âsecond useâ in-band alternative service directive imbedded in the HTTPS protocol exchange, which appears to be predominately used by the Chrome browser, and the DNS HTTPS trigger, which appears to be predominately used by the Safari browser.

data.title: Flux is a high-performance, zero-copy message transport library for Rust
data.author: ziyasal
data.article_summary: Flux 是一个为 Rust 设计的高性能、零拷贝消息传输库，适用于超低延迟、高吞吐量的应用。它借鉴了 LMAX Disruptor 和 Aeron 的设计模式，并进行了现代 Rust 优化。Flux 使用无锁、零拷贝的环形缓冲区（Ring Buffer），支持多生产者、多消费者模型，并通过多种性能优化手段（如 SIMD 数据拷贝、硬件 CRC32、NUMA 感知内存分配等）提升效率。其架构支持 IPC、UDP 和可靠 UDP 传输，并提供易用和高效的 API 示例，适合对性能要求苛刻的场景。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Flux库的特点和设计目标

不同观点：
• 支持观点（可能由[ziyasal]持有）：Flux是一个高性能、零拷贝的消息传输库，专为需要超低延迟和高吞吐量的应用设计。它借鉴了LMAX Disruptor和Aeron等知名项目的模式和实践，并结合了现代Rust的优化。这个观点强调了Flux的技术优越性和其在特定应用场景（如金融交易系统）中的潜在价值。

• 技术细节关注（可能由其他开发者提出）：Flux的实现依赖于先进的编程技术和优化，例如零拷贝（zero-copy）技术，这可以显著减少内存拷贝操作带来的开销，提高整体性能。该观点关注于Flux的技术实现细节及其带来的性能优势。

• 使用场景讨论（可能由实际应用者提出）：Flux适用于需要超低延迟和高吞吐量的应用场景，如高频交易、实时数据流处理等。这个观点讨论了Flux的具体应用场景，并暗示其在特定行业中的实用价值。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：虽然Flux的技术优势被强调，但也有开发者可能会质疑其实际应用中的稳定性和易用性，特别是在与已有解决方案（如LMAX Disruptor和Aeron）的比较中，是否能提供显著的性能提升和更低的延迟。

• 其他值得注意的讨论点：有开发者可能会讨论Flux在Rust生态系统中的定位，以及它如何与现有的消息传输库（如Crossbeam、Tokio等）竞争或互补。此外，Flux的零拷贝技术在实际应用中可能带来的复杂性和内存管理挑战也值得关注。

44616472.article_summary: Flux 是一个为 Rust 设计的高性能、零拷贝消息传输库，适用于超低延迟、高吞吐量的应用。它借鉴了 LMAX Disruptor 和 Aeron 的设计模式，并进行了现代 Rust 优化。Flux 使用无锁、零拷贝的环形缓冲区（Ring Buffer），支持多生产者、多消费者模型，并通过多种性能优化手段（如 SIMD 数据拷贝、硬件 CRC32、NUMA 感知内存分配等）提升效率。其架构支持 IPC、UDP 和可靠 UDP 传输，并提供易用和高效的 API 示例，适合对性能要求苛刻的场景。

data.title: How AI Vibe Coding Is Destroying Junior Developers' Careers
data.author: namanyayg
data.article_summary:
2025年，科技行业面临严重危机，已有超过94,000名科技工作者被解雇。尤其是初级开发人员，面临巨大挑战。据《印度时报》报道，美国软件开发岗位减少了70%以上，新毕业生很难进入科技行业。在严峻的就业市场中，许多新开发人员转向“氛围编码”（vibe coding），即利用AI构建应用而无需学习编码。这种方法造就了一批缺乏基本技能的“伪开发人员”，他们无法在竞争激烈的行业中生存。

“氛围编码”依赖AI生成代码，开发人员不写代码也不调试，直到“感觉对了”为止。这种方法跳过了学习过程，导致开发人员在遇到问题时只会依赖AI，形成恶性循环。研究显示，使用AI工具的开发人员生产力实际下降了19%，但他们自己却认为提高了20%。这种认知与现实的巨大差距表明，AI对成熟复杂项目的开发可能适得其反。

一个独立开发人员通过氛围编码创建SaaS产品，最终因无法调试和维护代码，项目失败。专家警告，随着更多公司使用AI生成代码，类似问题将频繁出现。

44618243.article_content:
The tech industry is facing a massive crisis in 2025.
Over 94,000 tech workers have already been laid off across 150 companies
this year alone. For junior developers, the situation is especially challenging. According to a
Times of India report
, software developer job openings in the U.S. have shrunk by over 70%, making it increasingly difficult for new graduates to break into tech.
In this tough job market, many new developers are turning to "
vibe coding."
This is a shortcut that promises to build applications using AI without actually learning to code. But this solution is making the problem worse. It's creating a generation of
pseudo-developers
who lack the basic skills needed to survive in an increasingly competitive industry.
The Vibe Coding Trap: A False Promise
Vibe coding describes a philosophy where developers "
fully give into the vibes, embrace exponentials, and forget that the code even exists.
" Originally created by Andrej Karpathy for throwaway weekend projects, the term has been hijacked by those promoting it as a real development approach.
In practice, vibe coding means using AI models to build your entire application without writing a single line of code yourself. When something breaks, you don't debug. You just keep asking the AI until it "feels right." As one developer explains: "
It's coding without coding.
You use AI models to build your entire app.
You don't write a single line yourself, not even for debugging.
"
This creates what we might call "the new tutorial hell." Unlike traditional learning where you at least absorbed concepts while watching tutorials, vibe coding skips the learning process entirely. You hit a problem, throw it at an AI, get a working solution, ship it quickly, then repeat the same cycle tomorrow when you face a similar issue.
The appeal is obvious, especially for newcomers facing a brutal job market. Why spend years learning complex programming languages when you can just describe what you want in plain English? The promise sounds amazing: no technical knowledge required, just explain your vision and watch the AI build it.
The illusion of Productivity: What the Data Actually Says?
Recent research
reveals a shocking disconnect between perception and reality when it comes to AI coding productivity. A rigorous METR study conducted in 2025 tracked
16 experienced developers
from major open-source projects as they completed 246 real-world coding tasks. The results were startling: developers using AI tools experienced a 19% decrease in productivity compared to working without AI assistance.
Even more concerning, the developers themselves were completely unaware of this slowdown.
They estimated that AI had increased their productivity by 20%
,
while the actual data showed the opposite
. This represents a massive 39-point gap between perception and reality, suggesting that many glowing reports about AI productivity gains may be fundamentally flawed.
The study was conducted as a randomized controlled trial under real-world conditions, with tasks randomly assigned to "
AI Allowed
" or
"AI Disallowed
" categories. Developers spent substantial time reviewing AI-generated code, with only 39% of AI code generations being accepted. Much of the supposed time savings from AI was offset by the need to prompt, wait for responses, review output, and often discard flawed code entirely.
This research challenges the widespread belief that AI tools are universally boosting developer productivity.
While AI may help with certain types of tasks, the study suggests that for experienced developers working on mature, complex codebases, these tools may actually be counterproductive. The gap between what developers think is happening and what's actually happening raises serious questions about how we're measuring and understanding AI's impact on software development.
When Vibe Coding Fails: The Catastrophic Failures
The most documented failure involves an indie developer who built a SaaS product entirely through vibe coding. Initially celebrating on social media that his "saas was built with Cursor, zero hand written code," the story quickly turned dark.
Source
Within weeks, disaster struck. The developer reported that "random things are happening, maxed out usage on api keys, people bypassing the subscription, creating random shit on db." Being non-technical, he couldn't debug the security breaches or understand what was going wrong. The application was eventually shut down permanently after he admitted "Cursor keeps breaking other parts of the code."
This failure illustrates the core problem with vibe coding:
it produces developers who can generate code but can't understand, debug, or maintain it. When AI-generated code breaks, these developers are helpless.

data.title: EPA shutters its scientific research arm
data.author: MPSFounder
data.article_summary: 美国环保署（EPA）宣布关闭其科学部门——研究与开发办公室（ORD），以节省7.488亿美元。该部门拥有超过1500名员工，负责关键的环境污染研究。此次关闭是机构重组的一部分，EPA员工总数已从2025年1月的16,155人减少到12,488人，减幅达22%。多数ORD员工通过新闻得知此消息，尚未收到正式通知。一些员工将被调任，其余可能离职。由于科学岗位减少，一些员工考虑赴海外工作。前EPA官员批评此举危及公共健康和环境监督，可能导致更严重的污染和经济负担。ORD研究涵盖多个领域，如“永久化学品”PFAS、水传播疾病和儿童哮喘的环境因素等。

. More than 1,500 employees, including scientists and researchers, are dispersed across the country at
11 different locations
, but the bulk are based at the EPA's headquarters in Washington, D.C., and at a large scientific facility in Research Triangle Park, North Carolina.
Eliminating the office will bring $748.8 million in savings, according to a news release from the agency.
The EPA had 16,155 employees back in January 2025, but following voluntary retirements, dismissals, and other reduction in force (RIF) actions, it is now down to 12,488 employees, the agency said in its release Friday, a reduction of about 22% of its staff. The staffing cuts include 3,201 employees who took the Trump administration's so-called "
Fork in the Road
" deferred resignation program, as well as those who took early retirement.
"Under President Trump's leadership, EPA has taken a close look at our operations to ensure the agency is better equipped than ever to deliver on our core mission of protecting human health and the environment while Powering the Great American Comeback," EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin said in a statement Friday. "This reduction in force will ensure we can better fulfill that mission while being responsible stewards of your hard-earned tax dollars."
It was anticipated that ORD would be impacted,
according to earlier documents that outlined the agency's RIF plans
. Back in March, the documents indicated that somewhere between 50% to 75% of ORD employees would not be retained, the majority of them leading scientists in their field of research.
A source inside ORD told CBS News Friday that employees found out about the reduction in force via the press release that was sent out to the public, and has not received any formal communication from the agency about what will happen next.
"A friend texted me the press release," the source told CBS News, "that is how I found out."
According to the source, most employees are anxiously checking their email, waiting to see if they'll be reassigned to another program office, or impacted by the reduction.
Some ORD employees have already received notification that they have been reassigned, while most wait to learn their fate. In May, ORD employees were told they would be contacted by other programs inside the agency to discuss potential, lateral moves. But according to the source, it now appears that impacted individuals won't get much of a choice: either take the reassignment if one is offered, or leave the agency.
"I don't think I can stay in the U.S.," one source told CBS News, "there are no jobs here."
Because of cuts to the federal workforce and cuts to scientific research, there are very few scientific positions available in the U.S., and some are now contemplating work abroad.
"Today's cuts dismantle one of the world's most respected environmental health research organizations," said Jennifer Orme-Zavaleta, former EPA principal deputy assistant administrator for science, in a statement. "EPA's science office has long been recognized internationally for advancing public health protections through rigorous science. Reducing its workforce under the guise of cost savings is both misleading and dangerous. This does
not
save taxpayers money; it simply shifts costs to hospitals, families and communities left to bear the health and economic consequences of increased pollution and weakened oversight. The people of this country are not well served by these actions. They are left more vulnerable."
The ORD's research touches on a range of issues from PFAS, often referred to as "forever chemicals," to water-bourne diseases, soot in the air, and environmental factors that contribute to childhood asthma, Orme-Zavaleta said.
It is made up of six major research program offices, per its website, that include
Air, Climate, and Energy
,
Chemical Safety for Sustainability
,
Health and Environmental Risk Assessment
,
Homeland Security
,
Safe and Sustainable Water Resources
and
Sustainable and Healthy Communities
.
It also includes four major research labs including the
Center for Computational Toxicology and Exposure (CCTE)
, the
Center for Environmental Measurement and Modeling (CEMM)
, the
Center for Environmental Solutions and Emergency Response (CESER)
and the
Center for Public Health and Environmental Assessment (CPHEA)
.

data.title: lsr: ls with io_uring
data.author: mpweiher
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了作者实现的一个比传统 `ls` 更快的文件列表工具 `lsr`，它使用了作者的 IO 库 `ourio`，通过 io_uring 进行大量 IO 操作，从而大幅减少系统调用次数。根据基准测试，`lsr` 比其他类似工具（如 `ls`, `eza`, `lsd` 等）速度更快，系统调用次数少一个数量级。`lsr` 通过批量处理 `stat` 调用和减少动态内存分配来优化性能，且由于静态链接，减少了 libc 相关的开销。文章还提到排序是主要工作负载之一，并表示使用 io_uring 显著优化了系统调用。项目使用了 `tangled.sh` 进行开发，并鼓励贡献代码和反馈。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕使用 io_uring 优化的 `ls` 命令替代方案的性能、实用性及技术细节的讨论。

不同观点：
• 作者 [rockorager] 介绍了项目的技术实现，并提供了进一步的技术文档链接，侧重于 io_uring 的应用及其性能提升。
• [ninkendo] 关注项目在不可靠网络环境下（如NFS服务器）的表现，质疑 io_uring 是否能缓解 NFS 设计中的固有缺陷，特别是在处理中断连接时的表现。
• [SillyUsername] 支持 io_uring 的广泛应用，通过实际例子（如 nvme 硬盘速度提升）说明其优势，并希望更多命令行工具采用 io_uring。
• [Imustaskforhelp] 对项目的功能表示赞赏，但提到与现有工具 `eza` 相比，`lsr` 在文件类型识别和颜色显示方面有所不足，同时提出对更多工具（如 `cat`）的需求。
• [maplant] 认为 io_uring 带来的性能提升在实际使用中（如列出10,000个文件）并不明显，因此对切换工具的必要性提出质疑，更关注其教学和演示价值。
• [swiftcoder] 对 io_uring 减少系统调用次数但仅带来2倍速度提升表示疑惑，质疑性能提升的实际效果。
• [michaelcampbell] 对项目的实用性持怀疑态度，认为 `ls` 的速度从未成为其使用中的问题，但对项目作为学习和趣味应用表示认可。

补充讨论：
• [the8472] 指出 io_uring 不支持 `getdents`，因此其主要优势在于批量 `stat` 操作，并提出如果能同时处理多个 `getdents` 请求会更有益。
• [jasonjmcghee] 对项目中图标支持的文件类型选择提出质疑，指出某些常见文件类型（如 `.c`, `.h`）没有图标。
• [adgjlsfhk1] 对 uutils 项目的性能表现感到失望，认为其是推动核心工具现代化的希望，但目前表现不如 GNU。
• [pvtmert] 通过 `strace` 分析 `lsd` 的行为，发现其多次调用 `clock_gettime`，猜测可能与时间计算相关。
• [tln] 提到文件系统性能的改进，指出现代文件系统在处理大量文件时的表现更好，并回忆过去在 ext2 文件系统上的经验。
• [quibono] 对 Zig 语言的内存分配机制提出疑问，关注其在实际应用中的使用方式。
• [Lockal] 提供了一个相关任务的链接，讨论 io_uring 在 uutils 项目中的应用潜力。
• [buybackoff] 提出一个与主题略微偏离的问题，询问 io_uring 在企业级服务器上的具体性能提升数值，特别是针对网络延迟的优化效果。

争议焦点：
• io_uring 是否能有效缓解 NFS 等不可靠网络服务的问题。
• 使用 io_uring 带来的性能提升是否值得在实际应用中替换传统工具。
• `lsr` 工具在文件类型识别和颜色显示方面的不足。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 对 Zig 语言内存分配机制的讨论。
• 对 uutils 项目性能表现的批评和期望。
• 对 io_uring 在企业级环境中的具体性能表现的询问。

44604050.article_content:
As an excercise in syscall golf, I wrote an implementation of
ls(1)
which uses my IO library,
ourio
to perform as much of the IO as possible. What I ended up with is something that is faster than any version or alternative to
ls
I tested, and also performs an
order of magnitude fewer syscalls
. I’m calling it
lsr
. Let’s start with the benchmarks, then we’ll see how we got there.
Benchmarks

hyperfine
on a directory of
n
plain files.

Syscalls

strace -c
on a directory of
n
plain files. (Lower is better)

How we got there
Let’s start with how
lsr
works. To list directory contents, we basically have 3 stages to the program:
Parse args
Gather data
Print data
All of the IO involved happens in the second step. Wherever possible,
lsr
utilizes io_uring to pull in the data it needs. To get to that point, it means that we open the target directory with io_uring, if we need local time, user data, or group data, we open (and read) those files with io_uring. We do all
stat
calls via io_uring, and as needed we do the equivalent of an
lstat
via io_uring. In practice, this means that the number of syscalls we have should be drastically smaller than equivalent programs because we are able to batch the
stat
syscall. The results clearly show this…
lsr
has at least an order of magnitude fewer syscalls than it’s closest equivalent, being
uutils ls
.
We also use the zig stdlib StackFallbackAllocator. This let’s
lsr
allocate memory it needs up front, but fallback to a different allocator when it’s exhausted the fixed allocation. We allocate 1MB up front, which is more than enough for typical usage. This further reduces syscalls by reducing mmap usage.
As a result of working directly with io_uring, we also bypass several libc related pitfalls. Namely, we have no dynamic linking -
ls
has some considerable overhead in loading libc and related libraries…but it also has the benefit of having locale support.
lsr
does not boast such a feature. Despite being statically linked,
lsr
is still smaller than GNU
ls
: 138.7KB vs 79.3KB when built with ReleaseSmall.
Anomolies and Thoughts
I have no idea what
lsd
is doing. I haven’t read the source code, but from viewing it’s
strace
, it is calling
clock_gettime
around 5 times
per file
. Why? I don’t know. Maybe it’s doing internal timing of steps along the way?
Sorting ends up being a massive part of the workload. I suspect this is where
uutils ls
is getting slowed down, since it is doing pretty good on a syscall basis.
lsr
spends about 30% of it’s runtime sorting, the rest is the IO loop.
This ended up being a pretty fun project to write, and didn’t take too much time either. I am shocked at how much io_uring can be used to reduce syscalls…
ls
is a pretty basic example but you can only imagine how much of an effect this would have on something like a server.
Also - I’m using
tangled.sh
for this project. They have a really cool idea, and I want to see how the PR workflow is so…if you have any bugs or changes, please visit the
repo
. All you need is an atproto account + app password. I suspect more icons will be needed, feel free to make an issue for icon requests!
